sentences.zh: 錢唐，字惟明，象山人。

translations.literal: Qian Tang, courtesy name Weiming, was a native of Xiangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Tang, courtesy name Weiming, was a native of Xiangshan.

sentences.zh: 博學敦行。

translations.literal: He was broadly learned and earnest in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned and earnest in conduct.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，舉明經。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu, he was recommended on the classics examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1 (1368), he was recommended on the classics examination.

sentences.zh: 對策稱旨，特授刑部尚書。

translations.literal: His policy responses pleased the throne, and he was specially appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His policy responses pleased the emperor, and he was specially appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 二年詔孔廟春秋釋奠，止行於曲阜，天下不必通祀。

translations.literal: In the second year an edict on the spring and autumn sacrifices at the Confucian temples stated that they were to be held only at Qufu and need not be observed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year an edict on the spring and autumn sacrifices at Confucian temples ruled that they were to be held only at Qufu and need not be observed empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 唐伏闕上疏言：「孔子垂教萬世，天下共尊其教，故天下得通祀孔子，報本之禮不可廢。

translations.literal: Tang prostrated himself at the palace gate and submitted a memorial saying: "Confucius handed down teaching for ten thousand generations, and all under Heaven jointly honor his teaching; therefore all under Heaven may jointly sacrifice to Confucius, and the ritual of repaying the root must not be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Tang prostrated himself at the palace gate and submitted a memorial saying, "Confucius handed down teaching for ten thousand generations, and the empire jointly honors his teaching; therefore the empire may jointly sacrifice to Confucius, and the ritual of repaying the root must not be abolished.

sentences.zh: 」侍郎程徐亦疏言：「古今祀典，獨社稷、三皇與孔子通祀。

translations.literal: " Vice Minister Cheng Xu also submitted a memorial saying: "In sacrificial canons ancient and modern, only the altars of soil and grain, the Three Sovereigns, and Confucius receive sacrifices throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: " Vice Minister Cheng Xu also submitted a memorial saying, "In sacrificial canons ancient and modern, only the altars of soil and grain, the Three Sovereigns, and Confucius receive sacrifices throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 天下民非社稷、三皇則無以生，非孔子之道則無以立。

translations.literal: The people of all under Heaven, without the altars of soil and grain and the Three Sovereigns, have no means to live; without the Way of Confucius, have no means to stand.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the empire, without the altars of soil and grain and the Three Sovereigns, have no means to live; without the Way of Confucius, have no means to stand upright.

sentences.zh: 堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武、周公，皆聖人也。

translations.literal: Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou were all sages.
translations.idiomatic: Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, King Wu, and the Duke of Zhou were all sages.

sentences.zh: 然發揮三綱五常之道，載之於經，儀範百王，師表萬世，使世愈降而人極不墜者，孔子力也。

translations.literal: Yet it was Confucius's power that brought forth the Way of the Three Bonds and Five Constants, recorded it in the classics, made it the model for a hundred kings and the teacher for ten thousand generations, and kept the human pole from falling though the age grew ever lower.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it was through Confucius's power that the Way of the Three Bonds and Five Constants was brought forth, recorded in the classics, made the model for a hundred kings and the teacher for ten thousand generations, and the human pole kept from falling though the age grew ever lower.

sentences.zh: 孔子以道設教，天下祀之，非祀其人，祀其教也，祀其道也。

translations.literal: Confucius established teaching through the Way; all under Heaven sacrifice to him—not sacrificing to the man, but sacrificing to his teaching, sacrificing to his Way.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius established teaching through the Way; the empire sacrifices to him—not to the man, but to his teaching, to his Way.

sentences.zh: 今使天下之人，讀其書，由其教，行其道，而不得舉其祀，非所以維人心、扶世教也。

translations.literal: Now to make the people of all under Heaven read his books, follow his teaching, and practice his Way, yet not allow them to perform his sacrifice—this is not the means to sustain people's hearts and uphold the teaching of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Now to make the people of the empire read his books, follow his teaching, and practice his Way, yet not allow them to perform his sacrifice—this is not how to sustain people's hearts and uphold the teaching of the age.

sentences.zh: 」皆不聽。

translations.literal: " Both were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: " Both memorials went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃用其言。

translations.literal: After a long time, their words were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time, the court adopted their advice.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗覽《孟子》，至「草芥」「寇仇」語，謂：「非臣子所宜言」，議罷其配享。

translations.literal: The emperor once perused the Mencius and, coming to the passages on "grass and stubble" and "foe and enemy," said: "These are not words a subject should speak," and deliberated removing Mencius from shared sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once read the Mencius and, coming to the passages on treating tyrants like "grass and stubble" or "foe and enemy," said, "These are not words a subject should speak," and deliberated removing Mencius from shared sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 詔：「有諫者以大不敬論。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Whoever remonstrates shall be judged for great irreverence.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated, "Whoever remonstrates shall be judged for great irreverence.

sentences.zh: 」唐抗疏入諫曰：「臣為孟軻死，死有余榮。

translations.literal: " Tang submitted a defiant memorial remonstrating: "Your servant would die for Meng Ke and still have glory to spare.
translations.idiomatic: " Tang submitted a defiant memorial remonstrating, "Your servant would die for Mencius and still have glory to spare.

sentences.zh: 」時廷臣無不為唐危。

translations.literal: " At the time no court official failed to fear for Tang.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time every court official feared for Tang's life.

sentences.zh: 帝鑒其誠懇，不之罪。

translations.literal: The emperor perceived his sincerity and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor perceived his sincerity and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 孟子配享亦旋復。

translations.literal: Mencius's shared sacrifice was also soon restored.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius's place in shared sacrifice was also soon restored.

sentences.zh: 然卒命儒臣修《孟子節文》雲。

translations.literal: Yet in the end he ordered Confucian officials to compile the Excerpts from the Mencius.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end he ordered Confucian officials to compile the Excerpts from the Mencius.

sentences.zh: 唐為人強直。

translations.literal: Tang's character was forceful and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Tang was forceful and upright by nature.

sentences.zh: 嘗詔講《虞書》，唐陛立而講。

translations.literal: Once an edict ordered lectures on the Documents of Yu; Tang lectured standing on the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor ordered lectures on the Documents of Yu; Tang lectured while standing on the palace steps.

sentences.zh: 或糾唐草野不知君臣禮，唐正色曰：「以古聖帝之道陳於陛下，不跪不為倨。

translations.literal: Some impeached Tang as a rustic who did not know the rites between ruler and subject; Tang said with a stern countenance: "To set forth before Your Majesty the Way of the ancient sage emperors—not to kneel is not arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Some impeached Tang as a rustic ignorant of the rites between ruler and subject; Tang said sternly, "To set forth before Your Majesty the Way of the ancient sage emperors—not to kneel is not arrogance.

sentences.zh: 」又嘗諫宮中不宜揭武後圖。

translations.literal: " He also once remonstrated that it was improper to display in the palace a portrait of Empress Wu.
translations.idiomatic: " He also once remonstrated that it was improper to display in the palace a portrait of Empress Wu.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，待罪午門外竟日。

translations.literal: Having offended the imperial will, he awaited punishment outside the Meridian Gate for a whole day.
translations.idiomatic: Having offended the emperor, he awaited punishment outside the Meridian Gate for a whole day.

sentences.zh: 帝意解，賜之食，即命撤圖。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was appeased; he gave him food and at once ordered the portrait removed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented, gave him food, and at once ordered the portrait removed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，謫壽州，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he was demoted to Shouzhou, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was demoted to Shouzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 程徐，字仲能，鄞人。

translations.literal: Cheng Xu, courtesy name Zhongneng, was a native of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xu, courtesy name Zhongneng, was a native of Yin.

sentences.zh: 元名儒端學子也。

translations.literal: He was a son of the Yuan famous Confucian Duan Xue.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of the Yuan-dynasty Confucian master Duan Xue.

sentences.zh: 至正中，以明《春秋》知名。

translations.literal: In the Zhizheng era he became renowned for his mastery of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhizheng era he became renowned for his mastery of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 歷官兵部尚書，致仕。

translations.literal: He successively served as Minister of War and then retired.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of War and then retired from office.

sentences.zh: 明兵入元都，妻金抱二歲兒與女瓊赴井死。

translations.literal: When Ming troops entered the Yuan capital, his wife Jin, holding their two-year-old son and daughter Qiong, threw themselves into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming troops entered the Yuan capital, his wife Jin, holding their two-year-old son and daughter Qiong, threw themselves into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年，偕危素等自北平至京。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 2, together with Wei Su and others, he came from Beiping to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 2 (1369), together with Wei Su and others, he came from Beiping to the capital.

sentences.zh: 授刑部侍郎，進尚書，卒。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of Justice, promoted to Minister, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of Justice, promoted to Minister, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 徐精勤通敏，工詩文，有集傳於世。

translations.literal: Xu was diligent, penetrating, and quick; skilled in poetry and prose, he left a collected works transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was diligent, penetrating, and quick-witted; skilled in poetry and prose, he left a collected works that circulated after his death.

sentences.zh: 韓宜可，字伯時，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Han Yike, courtesy name Boshi, was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yike, courtesy name Boshi, was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 元至正中，行御史臺辟為掾，不就。

translations.literal: In the Yuan Zhizheng era the Branch Censorate recruited him as a clerk; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuan Zhizheng era the Branch Censorate recruited him as a clerk; he declined.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，薦授山陰教諭，轉楚府錄事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu, on recommendation he was appointed instructor at Shanyin and then transferred to recorder of the Chu princedom.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongwu, on recommendation he was appointed instructor at Shanyin and then transferred to recorder of the Chu princedom.

sentences.zh: 尋擢監察御史，彈劾不避權貴。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to investigating censor and impeached without shunning the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to investigating censor and impeached without shunning the powerful.

sentences.zh: 時丞相胡惟庸、御史大夫陳寧、中丞塗節方有寵於帝，嘗侍坐，從容燕語。

translations.literal: At the time Chancellor Hu Weiyong, Censor-in-Chief Chen Ning, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Tu Jie were in the emperor's favor; once, as they attended seated, they conversed at ease.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Chancellor Hu Weiyong, Censor-in-Chief Chen Ning, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Tu Jie enjoyed the emperor's favor; once, as they attended seated, they conversed at ease.

sentences.zh: 宜可直前，出懷中彈文，劾三人險惡似忠，奸佞似直，恃功怙寵，內懷反側，擢置臺端，擅作威福，乞斬其首以謝天下。

translations.literal: Yike stepped forward, drew from his bosom an impeachment memorial, and charged the three with being treacherous yet seeming loyal, wicked yet seeming upright, relying on merit and clinging to favor, harboring rebellion within, raised to the censorate summit and arrogating authority and blessings, begging that their heads be cut off to answer all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yike stepped forward, drew an impeachment memorial from his robe, and charged the three with being treacherous yet seeming loyal, wicked yet seeming upright, relying on merit and clinging to favor, harboring rebellion within, raised to the censorate and arrogating authority, begging that their heads be cut off to answer the empire.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「快口御史，敢排陷大臣耶！

translations.literal: The emperor said angrily: "Sharp-tongued censor—dare you slander and entrap great ministers!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said angrily, "Sharp-tongued censor—dare you slander and entrap great ministers!

sentences.zh: 」命下錦衣衛獄，尋釋之。

translations.literal: " He ordered him cast into the Brocade-Clad Guard prison, but soon released him.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered him cast into the Brocade-Clad Guard prison, but soon released him.

sentences.zh: 九年出為陜西按察司僉事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he went out as Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Shaanxi Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was posted as Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Shaanxi Surveillance Commission.

sentences.zh: 時官吏有罪者，笞以上悉謫屯鳳陽，至萬數。

translations.literal: At the time officials and clerks who had committed offenses, from beating upward, were all banished to labor at Fengyang, reaching tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: At the time officials and clerks guilty of offenses punishable by beating or more were all banished to labor at Fengyang, reaching tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 宜可疏，爭之曰：「刑以禁淫慝，一民軌，宜論其情之輕重，事之公私，罪之大小。

translations.literal: Yike submitted a memorial contending: "Punishment is to restrain excess and wickedness and unify the people's standards; one should weigh the lightness or heaviness of the circumstances, the public or private nature of the matter, and the greatness or smallness of the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Yike submitted a memorial contending, "Punishment is to restrain excess and wickedness and unify the people's standards; one should weigh the lightness or heaviness of the circumstances, the public or private nature of the matter, and the greatness or smallness of the crime.

sentences.zh: 今悉令謫屯，此小人之幸，君子殆矣。

translations.literal: Now to order all banished to labor—this is the petty man's good fortune and the gentleman's peril.
translations.idiomatic: Now to order all banished to labor—this is the petty man's good fortune and the gentleman's peril.

sentences.zh: 乞分別，以協眾心。

translations.literal: I beg that distinctions be made to harmonize the multitude's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that distinctions be made to harmonize popular sentiment.

sentences.zh: 」帝可之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved it.

sentences.zh: 已，入朝京師。

translations.literal: Later he entered the capital for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Later he entered the capital for audience.

sentences.zh: 會賜諸司沒官男女，宜可獨不受。

translations.literal: It happened that male and female persons from confiscated official households were bestowed on the various offices; Yike alone did not accept any.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that male and female persons from confiscated official households were bestowed on the various offices; Yike alone refused to accept any.

sentences.zh: 且極論：「罪人不孥，古之制也。

translations.literal: Moreover he argued at length: "Not extending punishment to the criminal's family was the ancient regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he argued at length, "Not extending punishment to the criminal's family was the ancient regulation.

sentences.zh: 有事隨坐，法之濫也。

translations.literal: To punish associates because of involvement in a case is an abuse of law.
translations.idiomatic: To punish associates because of involvement in a case is an abuse of law.

sentences.zh: 況男女，人之大倫，婚姻逾時，尚傷和氣。

translations.literal: Moreover, male and female are the great bond of humanity; when marriage passes its season, even that harms harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, male and female relations are the great bond of humanity; when marriage passes its season, even that harms social harmony.

sentences.zh: 合門連坐，豈聖朝所宜！

translations.literal: Punishing whole households by association—how can this befit a sage dynasty!
translations.idiomatic: Punishing whole households by association—how can this befit a sage dynasty!

sentences.zh: 」帝是其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved his words.

sentences.zh: 後坐事將刑，禦謹身殿親鞫之，獲免。

translations.literal: Later, when he was implicated in a matter and was to be punished, the emperor personally tried him in the Hall of Cultivating the Person and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he was implicated in a matter and faced punishment, the emperor personally tried him in the Hall of Cultivating the Person and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 復疏，陳二十余事，皆報可。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial setting forth more than twenty matters; all received approval.
translations.idiomatic: He again submitted a memorial setting forth more than twenty matters; all received approval.

sentences.zh: 未幾，罷歸。

translations.literal: Before long he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was dismissed and returned home.

sentences.zh: 已，復征至。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned again.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned again.

sentences.zh: 命撰祀鐘山、大江文；

translations.literal: He was ordered to compose texts for sacrifices at Zhongshan and the Great River;
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to compose texts for sacrifices at Zhongshan and the Great River;

sentences.zh: 諭日本、征烏蠻詔，皆稱旨，特授山西右布政使。

translations.literal: edicts instructing Japan and campaigning against Wuman—all pleased the throne, and he was specially appointed Right Administration Commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: edicts instructing Japan and campaigning against Wuman—all pleased the emperor, and he was specially appointed Right Administration Commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 尋以事安置雲南。

translations.literal: Soon, because of a matter, he was placed in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, because of a matter, he was placed in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 惠帝即位，用檢討陳性善薦，起雲南參政，入拜左副都御史，卒於官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui acceded, on the recommendation of Compiler Chen Xingshan he was raised as Administration Commissioner of Yunnan, entered the capital to receive appointment as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui acceded, on Compiler Chen Xingshan's recommendation he was raised as Administration Commissioner of Yunnan, entered the capital to receive appointment as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 是夜大星隕，櫪馬皆驚嘶，人謂：「宜可當之」雲。

translations.literal: That night a great star fell, and stable horses all startled and neighed; people said it portended Yike.
translations.idiomatic: That night a great star fell, and stable horses all startled and neighed; people said it portended Yike.

sentences.zh: 帝之建御史臺也，諸御史以敢言著者，自宜可外，則稱周觀政。

translations.literal: When the emperor established the Censorate, among the censors renowned for daring speech, apart from Yike, Zhou Guanzheng was named.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor established the Censorate, among the censors renowned for daring speech, apart from Yike, Zhou Guanzheng was named.

sentences.zh: 觀政亦山陰人。

translations.literal: Guanzheng was also from Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzheng was also from Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 以薦授九江教授，擢監察御史。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was appointed instructor at Jiujiang and then promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he was appointed instructor at Jiujiang and then promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 嘗監奉天門。

translations.literal: Once he supervised at the Gate of Revering Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Once he supervised at the Gate of Revering Heaven.

sentences.zh: 有中使將女樂入，觀政止之。

translations.literal: A eunuch was about to bring female musicians inside; Guanzheng stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch was about to bring female musicians inside; Guanzheng stopped him.

sentences.zh: 中使曰：「有命」，觀政執不聽。

translations.literal: The eunuch said: "There is an order"; Guanzheng held firm and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch said, "There is an order"; Guanzheng held firm and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 中使慍而入，頃之出報曰：「御史且休，女樂已罷不用。

translations.literal: The eunuch entered angrily; shortly he came out and reported: "Censor, rest yourself—the female musicians have already been dismissed and will not be used.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch entered angrily; shortly he came out and reported, "Censor, rest yourself—the female musicians have already been dismissed and will not be used.

sentences.zh: 」觀政又拒曰：「必面奉詔。

translations.literal: " Guanzheng again refused, saying: "I must receive the edict face to face.
translations.idiomatic: " Guanzheng again refused, saying, "I must receive the edict face to face.

sentences.zh: 」已而帝親出宮，謂之曰：「宮中音樂廢缺，欲使內家肄習耳。

translations.literal: " Before long the emperor came out of the palace in person and said to him: "Palace music had fallen into disuse; I merely wished the inner household to practice it.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long the emperor came out of the palace in person and said to him, "Palace music had fallen into disuse; I merely wished the inner household to practice it.

sentences.zh: 朕已悔之，御史言是也。

sentences.zh: 」左右無不驚異者。

translations.literal: Guanzheng rose through offices to Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzheng rose through offices to Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 前觀政者，有歐陽韶，字子韶，永新人。

translations.literal: Before Guanzheng there was Ouyang Shao, courtesy name Zishao, a native of Yongxin.
translations.idiomatic: Before Guanzheng there was Ouyang Shao, courtesy name Zishao, a native of Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 薦授監察御史。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 有詔：日命兩御史侍班。

translations.literal: There was an edict: each day two censors were ordered to attend in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: There was an edict that each day two censors were to attend in attendance.

sentences.zh: 韶嘗侍直，帝乘怒將戮人。

translations.literal: Shao once attended on duty; the emperor, in anger, was about to execute someone.
translations.idiomatic: Shao once attended on duty when the emperor, in anger, was about to execute someone.

sentences.zh: 他御史不敢言，韶趨跪殿廷下，倉卒不能措詞，急捧手加額，呼曰：「陛下不可！

translations.literal: The other censors dared not speak; Shao hurried forward, knelt below the palace hall, and in haste could not find words—he quickly clasped his hands to his forehead and cried: "Your Majesty, you must not!
translations.idiomatic: The other censors dared not speak; Shao hurried forward and knelt below the palace hall. Unable to find words in his haste, he clasped his hands to his forehead and cried, "Your Majesty, you must not!

translations.literal: " The emperor perceived Shao's plain sincerity and yielded.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor perceived Shao's plain sincerity and yielded.

sentences.zh: 未幾，致仕，卒於家。

translations.literal: Before long he retired and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he retired and died at home.

sentences.zh: 蕭岐，字尚仁，泰和人。

translations.literal: Xiao Qi, courtesy name Shangren, was a native of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Qi, courtesy name Shangren, was a native of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 五歲而孤，事祖父母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned at five, he served his grandparents and became known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at five, he served his grandparents and became known for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 有司屢舉不赴。

translations.literal: The authorities repeatedly recommended him, but he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities repeatedly recommended him, but he declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 洪武十七年，詔征賢良，強起之。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 17 an edict summoned the worthy; he was forcibly raised to office.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 17 (1384) an edict summoned the worthy; he was forcibly raised to office.

sentences.zh: 上十便書，大意謂：帝刑罰過中，訐告風熾。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial on ten conveniences; its gist was that the emperor's punishments were excessive and the wind of accusation ran hot.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial on ten reforms; its gist was that the emperor's punishments were excessive and the culture of accusation ran rampant.

sentences.zh: 請禁止實封以杜誣罔；

translations.literal: He asked that sealed denunciations be forbidden to stop false charges;
translations.idiomatic: He asked that sealed denunciations be forbidden to stop false charges;

sentences.zh: 依律科獄以信詔令。

translations.literal: and that cases be judged according to law to give credence to edicts.
translations.idiomatic: and that cases be judged according to law to give credence to edicts.

sentences.zh: 凡萬余言。

translations.literal: In all it ran to more than ten thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: In all it ran to more than ten thousand words.

sentences.zh: 召見，授潭王府長史。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, he was appointed Chief Administrator of the Tan princedom.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for audience, he was appointed Chief Administrator of the Tan princedom.

sentences.zh: 力辭，忤旨，謫雲南楚雄訓導。

translations.literal: He strenuously declined, offended the imperial will, and was demoted to Instructor at Chuxiong in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He strenuously declined, offended the emperor, and was demoted to Instructor at Chuxiong in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 岐即日行，遣騎追還。

translations.literal: Qi set out that very day; mounted messengers were sent to bring him back.
translations.idiomatic: Qi set out that very day; mounted messengers were sent to bring him back.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，改授陜西平涼。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was reassigned to Pingliang in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was reassigned to Pingliang in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 再歲致仕。

translations.literal: Two years later he retired.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he retired.

sentences.zh: 復召與錢宰等考定《書》傳。

translations.literal: He was again summoned, and with Qian Zai and others examined and fixed the transmitted text of the Documents.
translations.idiomatic: He was again summoned, and with Qian Zai and others examined and fixed the transmitted text of the 《Documents》.

sentences.zh: 賜幣鈔，給驛歸。

translations.literal: He was granted silk and paper money and given post-horses for his return.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted silk and paper money and given post-horses for his return.

sentences.zh: 嘗輯《五經要義》；

translations.literal: He once compiled the Essentials of the Five Classics;
translations.idiomatic: He once compiled the Essentials of the Five Classics;

sentences.zh: 又取《刑統八韻賦》，引律令為之解，合為一集。

translations.literal: and also took the Eight-Rhyme Rhapsody on the Penal Code, citing statutes and ordinances to explain it, and combined them into one collection.
translations.idiomatic: and also took the Eight-Rhyme Rhapsody on the Penal Code, citing statutes and ordinances to explain it, and combined them into one collection.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「天下之理本一，出乎道必入乎刑。

translations.literal: He once said: "The principle of all under Heaven is fundamentally one: what issues from the Way must enter into punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "The principle of the empire is fundamentally one: what issues from the Way must enter into punishment.

sentences.zh: 吾合二書，使觀者有所省也。

translations.literal: I join the two books so that readers may gain insight.
translations.idiomatic: I join the two books so that readers may gain insight.

sentences.zh: 」學者稱「正固先生」。

translations.literal: " Scholars called him Master Zhenggu.
translations.idiomatic: " Scholars called him Master Zhenggu.

sentences.zh: 當是時，太祖治尚剛嚴，中外凜凜，奉法救過不給。

translations.literal: At that time Taizu governed with stern severity; within and without all were in awe, and keeping the law and remedying faults left no surplus.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Taizu governed with stern severity; within and without the court all stood in awe, and keeping the law and remedying faults left no surplus of effort.

sentences.zh: 而岐所上書過切直，帝不為忤。

translations.literal: Yet Qi's submitted memorial was excessively blunt and direct, and the emperor was not offended.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qi's memorial was excessively blunt and direct, and the emperor was not offended.

sentences.zh: 厥後以言被超擢者，有門克新。

translations.literal: Afterward, among those raised and promoted for their words was Men Kexin.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, among those raised and promoted for their words was Men Kexin.

sentences.zh: 克新，鞏昌人。

translations.literal: Kexin was a native of Gongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Kexin was a native of Gongchang.

sentences.zh: 泰州教諭也。

translations.literal: He was an instructor at Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was an instructor at Taizhou.

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when his term was complete, he came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, when his term was complete, he came to court.

sentences.zh: 召問經史及政治得失。

translations.literal: He was summoned and questioned on the classics, histories, and the gains and losses of government.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and questioned on the classics, histories, and the gains and losses of government.

sentences.zh: 克新直言無隱。

translations.literal: Kexin spoke straight without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Kexin spoke frankly without concealment.

sentences.zh: 授贊善。

translations.literal: He was appointed Instructor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Instructor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時紹興王俊華以善文辭，亦授是職。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Junhua of Shaoxing, skilled in literary composition, was also given this post.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Junhua of Shaoxing, skilled in literary composition, was also given this post.

sentences.zh: 上諭吏部曰：「左克新，右俊華，重直言也。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed the Ministry of Personnel: "Kexin on the left, Junhua on the right—I value straight speech.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed the Ministry of Personnel, "Kexin on the left, Junhua on the right—I value straight speech.

sentences.zh: 」初，教官給由至京，帝詢民疾苦。

translations.idiomatic: " Earlier, when instructors brought their credentials to the capital, the emperor inquired into the people's hardships.

translations.idiomatic: Wu Congquan of Kelan and Zhang Huan of Shanyin both said, "Your servant's duty is to instruct scholars; civil affairs are not our concern.

translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said angrily, "In Song, Hu Yuan as professor at Suzhou and Huzhou taught both classical meaning and practical administration;

translations.idiomatic: in Han, Jia Yi and Dong Zhongshu both rose from the fields and set forth the affairs of the age;

translations.idiomatic: in Tang, Ma Zhou, though he could not see Taizong in person, still taught military officials to speak on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 今既集朝堂，朕親詢問，俱無以對，誌聖賢之道者固如是乎！

translations.literal: Now that you are gathered in court and I personally inquire, you all have nothing to answer—is this how those who record the Way of sages and worthies behave!
translations.idiomatic: Now that you are gathered in court and I personally inquire, you all have nothing to answer—is this how those who record the Way of sages and worthies behave!

sentences.zh: 」命竄之邊方。

translations.literal: " He ordered them banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered them banished to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 且榜諭天下學校，使為鑒戒。

translations.literal: Moreover he posted notices to schools throughout the realm to take this as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he posted notices to schools throughout the realm to take this as a warning.

sentences.zh: 至是克新以亮直見重。

translations.literal: By this time Kexin was esteemed for his bright integrity.
translations.idiomatic: By this time Kexin was esteemed for his bright integrity.

sentences.zh: 不數年，擢禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Within a few years he was promoted to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he was promoted to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 尋引疾，命太醫給藥物，不輟其奉。

translations.literal: Soon he pleaded illness; the emperor ordered the imperial physicians to supply medicine and did not cut off his salary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he pleaded illness; the emperor ordered the imperial physicians to supply medicine and did not cut off his salary.

sentences.zh: 及卒，命有司護喪歸葬。

translations.literal: When he died, he ordered the relevant offices to escort the coffin home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he ordered the relevant offices to escort the coffin home for burial.

sentences.zh: 馮堅，不知何許人，為南豐典史。

translations.literal: Feng Jian—of unknown origin—served as clerk of Nanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jian—of unknown origin—served as clerk of Nanfeng.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十四年上書言九事：「一曰養聖躬。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 24 he submitted a memorial on nine matters: "First, nurturing the sage person.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 24 (1391) he submitted a memorial on nine matters: "First, nurturing the sage person.

sentences.zh: 請清心省事，不與細務，以為民社之福。

translations.literal: I ask that Your Majesty clear the mind and reduce affairs, not engaging in petty matters, for the blessing of the people's altars.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty clear the mind and reduce affairs, not engaging in petty matters, for the blessing of the people's altars.

sentences.zh: 二曰擇老成。

translations.literal: Second, selecting the mature and steady.
translations.idiomatic: Second, selecting the mature and steady.

sentences.zh: 諸王年方壯盛，左右輔導。

translations.literal: The princes are in their vigorous prime and need guidance at their sides.
translations.idiomatic: The princes are in their vigorous prime and need guidance at their sides.

sentences.zh: 願擇取老成之臣出為王官，使得直言正色，以圖匡救。

translations.literal: I wish that mature and steady ministers be chosen and sent out as princely officials, enabling them to speak straight and show a stern countenance, so as to seek correction and rescue.
translations.idiomatic: I wish that mature and steady ministers be chosen and sent out as princely officials, enabling them to speak straight and show a stern countenance, so as to seek correction and rescue.

sentences.zh: 三曰攘要荒。

translations.literal: Third, repelling the vital frontier wastes.
translations.idiomatic: Third, securing the vital frontier regions.

sentences.zh: 請務農講武，屯戍邊圉，以備不虞。

translations.literal: I ask that agriculture be stressed and arms practiced, with garrison farming on the border marches to guard against the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that agriculture be stressed and arms practiced, with garrison farming on the border marches to guard against the unforeseen.

sentences.zh: 四曰勵有司。

translations.literal: Fourth, encouraging the responsible officials.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, encouraging the responsible officials.

sentences.zh: 請得廉正有守之士，任以方面。

translations.literal: I ask that upright and principled men be obtained and entrusted with regional command.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that upright and principled men be obtained and entrusted with regional command.

sentences.zh: 旌別屬吏，具實以聞而黜陟之。

translations.literal: Commend and distinguish subordinate clerks, report the facts, and promote or demote accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Commend and distinguish subordinate clerks, report the facts, and promote or demote accordingly.

sentences.zh: 使人勇於自治。

translations.literal: This will make men bold in governing themselves.
translations.idiomatic: This will make men bold in governing themselves.

sentences.zh: 五曰褒祀典。

translations.literal: Fifth, honoring the sacrificial canon.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, honoring the sacrificial canon.

sentences.zh: 請敕有司采歷代忠烈諸臣，追加封謚，俾末俗有所興勸。

translations.literal: I ask that the relevant offices be ordered to gather loyal and heroic ministers of successive ages, add posthumous titles and enfeoffments, so that the degenerate age may have something to stir and encourage it.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the relevant offices be ordered to gather loyal and heroic ministers of successive ages, add posthumous titles and enfeoffments, so that the degenerate age may have something to stir and encourage it.

sentences.zh: 六曰省宦寺。

translations.literal: Sixth, reducing palace eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, reducing palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 晨夕密邇，其言易入，養成禍患而不自知。

translations.literal: Morning and evening they are close at hand; their words easily enter, and calamity is nurtured without one's knowing it.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening they are close at hand; their words easily enter, and calamity is nurtured without one's knowing it.

sentences.zh: 請裁去冗員，可杜異日陵替之弊。

translations.literal: I ask that redundant posts be cut away, which can stop the abuse of usurpation in days to come.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that redundant posts be cut away, which can stop the abuse of usurpation in days to come.

sentences.zh: 七曰易邊將。

translations.literal: Seventh, rotating border generals.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, rotating border generals.

sentences.zh: 假以兵柄，久在邊圉，多致縱佚。

translations.literal: Entrusted with military authority and long on the border marches, they often grow indulgent and lax.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with military authority and long on the border marches, they often grow indulgent and lax.

sentences.zh: 請時遷歲調，不使久居其任。

translations.literal: I ask that they be transferred at intervals and rotated yearly, not allowed to remain long in one post.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that they be transferred at intervals and rotated yearly, not allowed to remain long in one post.

sentences.zh: 不惟保全勛臣，實可防將驕卒惰、內輕外重之漸。

translations.literal: This would not only preserve meritorious ministers but truly guard against the gradual rise of arrogant generals and lazy soldiers, and of the inner being light while the outer grows heavy.
translations.idiomatic: This would not only preserve meritorious ministers but truly guard against arrogant generals and lazy soldiers, and against the inner court growing weak while the frontier grows strong.

sentences.zh: 八曰訪吏治。

translations.literal: Eighth, inquiring into officials' governance.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, inquiring into officials' governance.

sentences.zh: 廉幹之才，或為上官所忌，僚吏所嫉。

translations.literal: Men of integrity and capacity may be envied by superiors and resented by colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: Men of integrity and capacity may be envied by superiors and resented by colleagues.

sentences.zh: 上不加察，非激勸之道。

translations.literal: If the throne does not investigate, this is not the way to stir and encourage.
translations.idiomatic: If the throne does not investigate, this is not the way to stir and encourage merit.

sentences.zh: 請廣布耳目，訪察廉貪，以明黜陟。

translations.literal: I ask that ears and eyes be broadly deployed, integrity and greed investigated, and promotion and demotion made clear.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that ears and eyes be broadly deployed, integrity and greed investigated, and promotion and demotion made clear.

sentences.zh: 九曰增關防。

translations.literal: Ninth, increasing checkpoints and controls.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, increasing checkpoints and controls.

sentences.zh: 諸司以帖委胥吏，俾督所部，輒加箠楚，害及於民。

translations.literal: The various offices entrust notes to clerks, who supervise their jurisdictions and at once add beating with the cudgel, harm reaching the people.
translations.idiomatic: The various offices entrust notes to clerks, who supervise their jurisdictions and at once add beating with the cudgel, harm reaching the people.

sentences.zh: 請增置勘合以付諸司，聽其填寫差遣，事訖繳報，庶所司不輕發以病民，而庶務亦不致曠廢。

translations.literal: I ask that verification tallies be added and given to the offices, allowing them to fill in assignments; when matters end they are returned and reported—then the offices will not lightly issue orders to harm the people, yet routine affairs will not fall into neglect.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that verification tallies be added and given to the offices, allowing them to fill in assignments; when matters end they are returned and reported—then the offices will not lightly issue orders to harm the people, yet routine affairs will not fall into neglect.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，帝嘉之，稱其知時務，達事變。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised it, saying he understood the affairs of the age and grasped changes in circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised it, saying he understood the affairs of the age and grasped changes in circumstances.

sentences.zh: 又謂侍臣曰：「堅言惟調易邊將則未然。

translations.literal: He also said to attending ministers: "Of Jian's words, only the proposal to rotate border generals is not yet so.
translations.idiomatic: He also said to attending ministers, "Of Jian's words, only the proposal to rotate border generals is not yet so.

sentences.zh: 邊將數易，則兵力勇怯。

translations.literal: If border generals are frequently changed, then military strength grows brave or timid.
translations.idiomatic: If border generals are frequently changed, military strength grows uneven.

sentences.zh: 敵情出沒，出川形勝，無以備知。

translations.literal: Enemy movements, mountain passes and strategic terrain—none can be fully known.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy movements, mountain passes and strategic terrain—none can be fully known.

sentences.zh: 倘得趙充國、班超者，又何取數易為哉！

translations.literal: If one could obtain men like Zhao Chongguo or Ban Chao, why take frequent rotation!
translations.idiomatic: If one could obtain men like Zhao Chongguo or Ban Chao, why take frequent rotation!

sentences.zh: 」乃命吏部擢堅左僉都御史，在院頗持大體。

translations.literal: " He then ordered the Ministry of Personnel to promote Jian to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief; in the Censorate he largely upheld broad principle.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered the Ministry of Personnel to promote Jian to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief; in the Censorate he largely upheld broad principle.

sentences.zh: 其明年，卒於任。

translations.literal: The next year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 茹太素，澤州人。

translations.literal: Ru Taisu was a native of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Taisu was a native of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，鄉舉，上書稱旨，授監察御史。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 3 he passed the provincial examination; his submitted memorial pleased the throne, and he was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3 (1370) he passed the provincial examination; his submitted memorial pleased the emperor, and he was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 六年擢四川按察使，以平允稱。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Sichuan and was known for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Sichuan and was known for fairness.

sentences.zh: 七年五月召為刑部侍郎，上言：「自中書省內外百司，聽御史、按察使檢舉。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year he was summoned as Vice Minister of Justice and submitted a memorial: "From the Secretariat of State down through all inner and outer offices, let censors and surveillance commissioners investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventh year he was summoned as Vice Minister of Justice and submitted a memorial: "From the Secretariat of State down through all inner and outer offices, let censors and surveillance commissioners investigate and report.

sentences.zh: 而御史臺未有定考，宜令守院御史一體察核。

translations.literal: Yet the Censorate has no fixed evaluation; the resident censors should be ordered to inspect and verify as one body.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Censorate has no fixed evaluation; the resident censors should be ordered to inspect and verify as one body.

translations.literal: The clerks of the Scrutiny Office are few in number and can hardly audit the realm's money and grain; I ask that several posts be added, each divided into sections.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks of the Scrutiny Office are few in number and can hardly audit the realm's money and grain; I ask that several posts be added, each divided into sections.

sentences.zh: 在外省衛，凡會議軍民事，各不相合，致稽延。

translations.literal: In outer provinces and guards, whenever military and civil affairs are jointly discussed, the parties do not agree, causing delay.
translations.idiomatic: In outer provinces and guards, whenever military and civil affairs are jointly discussed, the parties do not agree, causing delay.

sentences.zh: 請用按察司一員糾正。

translations.literal: I ask that one member of the Surveillance Commission be used to correct this.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that one member of the Surveillance Commission be used to correct this.

sentences.zh: 」帝皆從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved all of it.

sentences.zh: 明年，坐累降刑部主事。

translations.literal: The next year, implicated in a case, he was demoted to Registrar of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, implicated in a case, he was demoted to Registrar of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 陳時務累萬言，太祖令中書郎王敏誦而聽之。

translations.literal: He set forth affairs of the age in tens of thousands of words; Taizu ordered Secretariat Attendant Wang Min to read it aloud while he listened.
translations.idiomatic: He set forth affairs of the age in tens of thousands of words; Taizu ordered Secretariat Attendant Wang Min to read it aloud while he listened.

sentences.zh: 中言：「才能之士，數年來幸存者百無一二，今所任率迂儒俗吏。

translations.literal: In the middle he said: "Men of talent—in recent years scarcely one or two in a hundred have survived; those now appointed are mostly pedantic Confucians and vulgar clerks.
translations.idiomatic: In the middle he said, "Men of talent—in recent years scarcely one or two in a hundred have survived; those now appointed are mostly pedantic Confucians and vulgar clerks.

sentences.zh: 」言多忤觸。

translations.literal: " His words mostly gave offense.
translations.idiomatic: " His words mostly gave offense.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，召太素面詰，杖於朝。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, summoned Taisu to face questioning, and had him beaten at court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry, summoned Taisu to face questioning, and had him beaten at court.

sentences.zh: 次夕，復於宮中令人誦之，得其可行者四事。

translations.literal: The next evening, again in the palace he had someone read it and found four matters that could be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The next evening, again in the palace he had someone read it and found four matters that could be carried out.

sentences.zh: 慨然曰：「為君難，為臣不易。

translations.literal: He said with emotion: "To be ruler is hard; to be minister is not easy.
translations.idiomatic: He said with emotion, "To be ruler is hard; to be minister is not easy.

sentences.zh: 朕所以求直言，欲其切於情事。

translations.literal: That is why I seek straight speech—I want it to cut close to real circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I seek straight speech—I want it to cut close to real circumstances.

sentences.zh: 文詞太多，便至熒聽。

translations.literal: Too many literary words, and it reaches the point of confusing the ear.
translations.idiomatic: Too many literary words, and it reaches the point of confusing the listener.

sentences.zh: 太素所陳，五百余言可盡耳。

translations.literal: What Taisu set forth could be fully stated in five hundred-odd words—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: What Taisu had to say could be said completely in five hundred-odd words.

sentences.zh: 」因令中書定奏對式，俾陳得失者無繁文。

translations.literal: " He thereupon ordered the Secretariat to fix a format for memorial replies, so that those who set forth gains and losses would not use verbose prose.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered the Secretariat to establish a format for memorial responses, so that those reporting what worked and what failed would not pad their submissions with ornate language.

sentences.zh: 摘太素疏中可行者下所司，帝自序其首，頒示中外。

translations.literal: He extracted from Taisu's memorial what could be carried out and sent it down to the responsible offices; the emperor himself wrote a preface at its head and promulgated it within and without the court.
translations.idiomatic: He picked out the feasible proposals from Taisu's memorial and sent them to the relevant offices; the emperor wrote a preface himself and issued the document throughout the court and the realm.

sentences.zh: 十年，與同官曾秉正先後同出為參政，而太素往浙江。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he and his colleague Zeng Bingzheng were successively dispatched together as Administrative Commissioners, while Taisu went to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, he and his colleague Zeng Bingzheng were both sent out as provincial administrators in turn, while Taisu was posted to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 尋以侍親賜還裏。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on account of attending to his parents, he was granted leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was granted leave to go home and care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 十六年召為刑部試郎中。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was summoned as Probationary Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was recalled to serve as a probationary bureau director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 居一月，遷都察院僉都御史。

translations.literal: After one month in office, he was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: After a month he was transferred to vice censor-in-chief of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 復降翰林院檢討。

translations.literal: Again he was demoted to Compiler in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted again, this time to compiler in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 十八年九月擢戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighteenth year he was promoted to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eighteenth year he was promoted to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 太素抗直不屈，屢瀕於罪，帝時宥之。

translations.literal: Taisu resisted straightly and would not submit; repeatedly he was on the verge of offense, and the emperor at times granted him pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Taisu was upright and unyielding, repeatedly on the verge of punishment, yet the emperor often spared him.

sentences.zh: 一日，宴便殿，賜之酒曰：「金杯同汝飲，白刃不相饒。

translations.literal: One day, at a banquet in the informal hall, he granted him wine and said: "The golden cup we drink together; the naked blade shows no mercy.
translations.idiomatic: One day, at a banquet in the informal hall, the emperor gave him wine and said, "We may share the golden cup, but the naked blade shows no mercy.

sentences.zh: 」太素叩首，即續韻對曰：「丹誠圖報國，不避聖心焦。

translations.literal: " Taisu kowtowed and immediately continued the rhyme in reply: "With crimson devotion I seek to repay the state, not shunning the sovereign heart's vexation.
translations.idiomatic: " Taisu kowtowed and immediately answered in matching verse: "With loyal devotion I seek to serve the state, not shrinking from Your Majesty's troubled heart.

sentences.zh: 」帝為惻然。

translations.literal: " The emperor was moved to compassion.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 未幾，謫御史，復坐排陷詹徽，與同官十二人俱鐐足治事。

translations.literal: Before long he was demoted to censor. Again convicted of framing Zhan Hui, he and twelve colleagues all wore fetters on their feet while conducting business.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was demoted to censor. He was convicted again of framing Zhan Hui, and he and twelve colleagues all had to conduct their duties in leg irons.

sentences.zh: 後竟坐法死。

translations.literal: In the end he was executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was put to death under the law.

sentences.zh: 曾秉正，南昌人。

translations.literal: Zeng Bingzheng was a native of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Bingzheng was from Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，薦授海州學正。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu, through recommendation he was appointed Instructor at Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Hongwu reign he was recommended and appointed instructor at Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 九年，以天變詔群臣言事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, on account of a celestial anomaly an edict summoned the ministers to speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, after a celestial anomaly, an edict called on the ministers to speak their minds.

sentences.zh: 秉正上疏數千言，大略曰：「古之聖君不以天無災異為喜，惟以祗懼天譴為心。

translations.literal: Bingzheng submitted a memorial of several thousand words, which in general said: "The sage rulers of antiquity did not rejoice when Heaven sent no calamities and anomalies; they took reverent fear of Heaven's reprimand as their heart.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzheng submitted a memorial several thousand words long, which in essence said, "The sage rulers of old did not rejoice when Heaven sent no omens of disaster; they lived in reverent fear of Heaven's rebuke.

sentences.zh: 陛下聖文神武，統一天下，天之付與，可謂盛矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is sage in culture and divine in martial prowess, having unified all under Heaven—the gift of Heaven may be called abundant indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is sage in learning and mighty in arms, and you have unified the realm; Heaven's gift to you could hardly be greater.

sentences.zh: 兵動二十余年，始得休息。

translations.literal: For more than twenty years arms were active; only then was there rest.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years war raged; only now has the realm found rest.

sentences.zh: 天之有心於太平亦已久矣；

translations.literal: Heaven's mind toward Great Peace has also long endured;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has long desired peace for the realm;

sentences.zh: 民之思治亦切矣。

translations.literal: the people's longing for good order is also keen.
translations.idiomatic: and the people long for good government with equal urgency.

sentences.zh: 創業與守成之政，大抵不同。

translations.literal: The policies of founding an enterprise and of preserving an achievement are in general not the same.
translations.idiomatic: The policies needed to build a dynasty and those needed to preserve one are, in general, not the same.

sentences.zh: 開創之初，則行富國強兵之術，用趨事赴功之人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of founding, one applies methods to enrich the state and strengthen the army, and employs men who hurry to affairs and rush to achievement.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding stage, one pursues policies to enrich the state and strengthen the army and appoints men who drive hard at tasks and deliver results.

sentences.zh: 大統既立，邦勢已固。

translations.literal: Once the great succession is established, the state's momentum is already firm.
translations.idiomatic: Once the dynasty is firmly established, the state's position is secure.

sentences.zh: 則普天之下，水土所生，人力所成，皆邦家倉庫之積；

translations.literal: Then all under Heaven—what water and earth produce, what human strength completes—all are accumulations in the state's granaries and storehouses;
translations.idiomatic: Then everything under Heaven, whether produced by land and water or completed by human labor, belongs to the state's stores;

sentences.zh: 乳哺之童，垂白之叟，皆邦家休養之人。

translations.literal: suckling children and white-haired old men—all are people whom the state nurtures and restores.
translations.idiomatic: from nursing infants to white-haired elders—all are people the state is bound to nurture and protect.

sentences.zh: 不患不富庶，惟保成業於永久為難耳。

translations.literal: One need not worry about not being wealthy and populous; only preserving the achieved enterprise forever is hard.
translations.idiomatic: There is no need to fear poverty or depopulation; the hard part is preserving what has been achieved for the long term.

sentences.zh: 於此之時，當盡革向之所為，何者足應天心，何者足慰民望，感應之理，其效甚速。

translations.literal: At such a time one ought fully to reform what was done before: what suffices to answer Heaven's mind, what suffices to comfort the people's hopes—the principle of resonance and response, its effect is very swift.
translations.idiomatic: At such a moment the court should thoroughly revise past practices, asking what will answer Heaven's intent and satisfy the people's hopes; the principle of moral resonance works quickly.

sentences.zh: 」又言天既有警，則變不虛生。

translations.literal: " He also said that since Heaven had already issued a warning, the anomaly was not born in vain.
translations.idiomatic: " He also argued that since Heaven had already sent a warning, the omen was not meaningless.

sentences.zh: 極論《大易》、《春秋》之旨。

translations.literal: He argued at length the purport of the 《Great Changes》 and the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》.
translations.idiomatic: He expounded at length on the meaning of the 《Great Changes》 and the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，召為思文監丞。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him and summoned him as Supervisor of the Siwen Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him and summoned him to serve as supervisor of the Siwen Directorate.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改刑部主事。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to Registrar of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to registrar in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 十年擢陜西參政。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to Administrative Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was promoted to administrative commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 會初置通政司，即以秉正為使。

translations.literal: When the Office of Transmission was first established, Bingzheng was immediately made its commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Office of Transmission was first created, Bingzheng was immediately appointed its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 在位數言事，帝頗優容之。

translations.literal: While in office he repeatedly spoke on affairs, and the emperor was rather lenient with him.
translations.idiomatic: While in office he repeatedly remonstrated, and the emperor was fairly indulgent toward him.

sentences.zh: 尋竟以忤旨罷。

translations.literal: Before long he was dismissed after all for contravening the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was dismissed for going against the emperor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 貧不能歸，鬻其四歲女。

translations.literal: Too poor to return home, he sold his four-year-old daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to make the journey home, he sold his four-year-old daughter.

sentences.zh: 帝聞大怒，置腐刑，不知所終。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he was greatly angered and imposed castration; his final end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he was furious and had him castrated; what became of him afterward is unknown.

sentences.zh: 李仕魯，字宗孔，濮人。

translations.literal: Li Shilu, courtesy name Zongkong, was a native of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shilu, styled Zongkong, was a native of Pu.

sentences.zh: 少穎敏篤學，足不窺戶外者三年。

translations.literal: In youth he was quick and clever and devoted to learning; for three years his feet did not cross the threshold outdoors.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was bright and diligent in study; for three years he never once stepped outside his door.

sentences.zh: 聞鄱陽朱公遷得宋朱熹之傳，往從之遊，盡受其學。

translations.literal: Hearing that Zhu Gongqian of Poyang had received the transmission of Song Neo-Confucian Zhu Xi, he went to study with him and fully received his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zhu Gongqian of Poyang had inherited the teaching of the Song master Zhu Xi, he went to study with him and mastered his doctrine in full.

sentences.zh: 太祖故知仕魯名，洪武中，詔求能為朱氏學者，有司舉仕魯。

translations.literal: Taizu had long known Shilu's name. During Hongwu an edict sought scholars able to practice the Zhu school; the responsible offices recommended Shilu.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had long known Shilu by reputation. During Hongwu an edict called for scholars versed in the Zhu school, and the local authorities recommended Shilu.

sentences.zh: 入見，太祖喜曰：「吾求子久，何相見晚也！

translations.literal: On entering audience, Taizu said with delight: "I have sought you long—why is our meeting so late!
translations.idiomatic: When he was received in audience, Taizu said with delight, "I have been looking for you for a long time—why have we met so late!

sentences.zh: 」除黃州同知。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Vice Prefect of Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed vice prefect of Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 曰：「朕姑以民事試子，行召子矣。

translations.literal: He said: "I shall for the moment test you with civil affairs; soon I shall summon you.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "For now I shall test you in civil administration; I shall summon you before long.

sentences.zh: 」期年，治行聞。

translations.literal: " After one year his governance became known.
translations.idiomatic: " After a year his record of governance became widely known.

sentences.zh: 十四年，命為大理寺卿。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was appointed chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 帝自踐阼後，頗好釋氏教。

translations.literal: Since ascending the throne, the emperor had been rather fond of the Buddhist teaching.
translations.idiomatic: After taking the throne, the emperor became quite devoted to Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 詔征東南戒德僧，數建法會於蔣山。

translations.literal: Edicts summoned precept-worthy monks of the southeast; Buddhist assemblies were repeatedly held on Mount Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts summoned eminent monks from the southeast, and Buddhist assemblies were repeatedly held on Mount Zhong.

sentences.zh: 應對稱旨者輒賜金礻闌袈裟衣，召入禁中，賜坐與講論。

translations.literal: Those whose replies pleased him were at once granted golden brocade kasaya robes, summoned into the inner palace, granted seats, and engaged in discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Those whose answers pleased him were immediately given golden brocade kasaya robes, summoned into the inner palace, seated beside him, and invited to discourse with him.

sentences.zh: 吳印、華克勤之屬，皆拔擢至大官，時時寄以耳目。

translations.literal: Men such as Wu Yin and Hua Keqin were all plucked out and promoted to high office, and from time to time entrusted as the emperor's eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Wu Yin and Hua Keqin were all promoted to high office and from time to time used as the emperor's eyes and ears.

sentences.zh: 由是其徒橫甚，讒毀大臣。

translations.literal: From this their followers grew extremely overbearing and slandered great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: As a result their followers grew brazen, slandering senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 舉朝莫敢言，惟仕魯與給事中陳汶輝相繼爭之。

translations.literal: The whole court dared not speak; only Shilu and Supervising Secretary Chen Wenhui successively contended against it.
translations.idiomatic: No one in court dared speak out; only Shilu and supervising secretary Chen Wenhui protested in succession.

sentences.zh: 汶輝疏言：「古帝王以來，未聞縉紳緇流，雜居同事，可以相濟者也。

translations.literal: Wenhui memorialized saying: "Since ancient emperors and kings, one has not heard of girdled officials and black-robed clergy mingling together in the same offices, able to help one another.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhui memorialized, saying, "Since antiquity there has never been a case in which court officials and Buddhist clergy mixed together in the same offices and managed to assist one another.

sentences.zh: 今勛舊耆德鹹思辭祿去位，而緇流憸夫乃益以讒間。

translations.literal: Today meritorious elders and venerable worthies all wish to resign their stipends and leave their posts, while black-robed villains only increase their slanderous intrigue.
translations.idiomatic: Today meritorious elders and venerable statesmen all wish to resign their stipends and leave office, while scheming monks only spread slander more freely.

sentences.zh: 如劉基、徐達之見猜，李善長、周德興之被謗，視蕭何、韓信，其危疑相去幾何哉？

translations.literal: As with Liu Ji's being suspected and Xu Da's being distrusted, Li Shanchang and Zhou Dexing being slandered—compared with Xiao He and Han Xin, how far apart are the peril and suspicion?
translations.idiomatic: Consider how Liu Ji came under suspicion, Xu Da was distrusted, and Li Shanchang and Zhou Dexing were slandered—compared with Xiao He and Han Xin, how much difference is there in the danger and distrust they faced?

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下於股肱心膂，悉取德行文章之彥，則太平可立致矣。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty, in your arms and thighs and heart and backbone, will entirely select men of outstanding virtue, conduct, and literary attainment—then Great Peace can be immediately attained.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty, in choosing the men closest to you, to appoint only those outstanding in virtue, conduct, and learning—then peace can be achieved at once.

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 諸僧怙寵者，遂請為釋氏創立職官。

translations.literal: The monks who relied on favor thereupon requested that official posts be created for the Buddhist church.
translations.idiomatic: The monks who enjoyed imperial favor then asked that official posts be created for the Buddhist clergy.

sentences.zh: 於是以先所置善世院為僧錄司。

translations.literal: Accordingly the previously established Shishi Bureau was made the Monastic Registry.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly the previously established Shishi Bureau was converted into the Monastic Registry.

sentences.zh: 設左、右善世、左、右闡教、左、右講經覺義等官，皆高其品秩。

translations.literal: Left and Right Shishi, Left and Right Expositors of Doctrine, Left and Right Lecturers on Scripture and Awakeners to Meaning, and other such posts were established, all with elevated rank grades.
translations.idiomatic: Posts such as left and right shishi, left and right expositors of doctrine, and left and right lecturers on scripture and awakeners to meaning were created, all with elevated rank.

sentences.zh: 道教亦然。

translations.literal: The same was true for Daoism.
translations.idiomatic: The same was done for Daoism.

sentences.zh: 度僧尼道士至逾數萬。

translations.literal: Ordained Buddhist monks and nuns and Daoist priests reached more than tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The number of ordained Buddhist monks and nuns and Daoist priests rose to more than tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 仕魯疏言：「陛下方創業，凡意指所向，即示子孫萬世法程，奈何舍聖學而崇異端乎！

translations.literal: Shilu memorialized: "Your Majesty is just founding the enterprise; every intention and direction becomes a model for ten thousand generations of descendants—how can you abandon sage learning and exalt heterodox teachings!
translations.idiomatic: Shilu memorialized, saying, "Your Majesty is still in the founding stage of the dynasty; every intention you set becomes a model for countless generations—how can you abandon sage learning and elevate heterodox teachings!

sentences.zh: 」章數十上，亦不聽。

translations.literal: " He submitted memorials dozens of times, and still the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " He submitted memorial after memorial, but the emperor still would not listen.

sentences.zh: 仕魯性剛介，由儒術起，方欲推明朱氏學，以辟佛自任。

translations.literal: Shilu was by nature stern and upright. Raised through Confucian learning, he was just then seeking to extend the Zhu school and took it upon himself to refute Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: Shilu was by nature stern and uncompromising. Having risen through Confucian learning, he was then seeking to promote the Zhu school and took it upon himself to oppose Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 及言不見用，遽請於帝前，曰：「陛下深溺其教，無惑乎臣言之不入也！

translations.literal: When his words went unheeded, he abruptly petitioned before the emperor, saying: "Your Majesty is deeply drowned in that teaching—no wonder my words do not enter!
translations.idiomatic: When his advice went unheeded, he suddenly addressed the emperor directly, saying, "Your Majesty is deeply immersed in that faith—no wonder my words fail to reach you!

sentences.zh: 還陛下笏，乞賜骸骨歸田裏。

translations.literal: I return Your Majesty's tablet and beg leave to grant my bones and return to my fields.
translations.idiomatic: I return Your Majesty's tablet and beg permission to retire to my home.

sentences.zh: 」遂置笏於地。

translations.literal: " He thereupon placed his tablet on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he set his court tablet on the ground.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，命武士捽搏之，立死階下。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, ordered guards to seize and beat him, and he died on the spot below the steps.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered guards to seize and beat him; he died instantly at the foot of the steps.

sentences.zh: 陳汶輝，字耿光，詔安人。

translations.literal: Chen Wenhui, courtesy name Gengguang, was a native of Zhao'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wenhui, styled Gengguang, was a native of Zhao'an.

sentences.zh: 以薦授禮科給事中，累官至大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: Through recommendation he was appointed Supervising Secretary in the Office of Rites; he rose through offices to Vice Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for office, he was appointed supervising secretary in the Office of Rites and eventually rose to vice chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 數言得失，皆切直。

translations.literal: He repeatedly spoke on gains and losses, all incisive and straight.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly spoke on policy, always with blunt candor.

sentences.zh: 最後忤旨，懼罪，投金水橋下死。

translations.literal: Finally he contravened the imperial intent; fearing punishment, he threw himself from beneath the Jinshui Bridge and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he offended the emperor; fearing punishment, he drowned himself beneath the Jinshui Bridge.

sentences.zh: 仕魯與汶輝死數歲，帝漸知諸僧所為多不法，有詔清理釋道二教雲。

translations.literal: Several years after Shilu and Wenhui died, the emperor gradually learned that the monks' conduct was largely unlawful, and an edict was issued to purge the two teachings of Buddhism and Daoism—or so it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Several years after Shilu and Wenhui died, the emperor gradually realized that the monks' conduct was largely unlawful, and an edict was issued to purge Buddhism and Daoism—or so it is said.

sentences.zh: 葉伯巨，字居升，寧海人。

translations.literal: Ye Boju, courtesy name Jusheng, was a native of Ninghai.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Boju, styled Jusheng, was a native of Ninghai.

sentences.zh: 通經術。

translations.literal: He mastered the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He was well versed in the classics.

sentences.zh: 以國子生授平遙訓導。

translations.literal: As a National University student he was appointed Instructor at Pingyao.
translations.idiomatic: As a student of the National University he was appointed instructor at Pingyao.

sentences.zh: 洪武九年星變，詔求直言。

translations.literal: In Hongwu's ninth year there was a stellar anomaly; an edict sought blunt speech.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Hongwu a stellar anomaly occurred, and an edict called for blunt counsel.

sentences.zh: 伯巨上書，略曰：

translations.literal: Boju submitted a letter, which in summary said:
translations.idiomatic: Boju submitted a memorial, which in summary said:

sentences.zh: 臣觀當今之事，太過者三：分封太侈也，用刑太繁也，求治太速也。

translations.literal: I observe that among present affairs three things are excessive: enfeoffment is too lavish, the use of punishments too numerous, and the quest for order too hasty.
translations.idiomatic: I observe three excesses in present policy: enfeoffment is too lavish, punishments are too frequent, and the pursuit of order is too hurried.

sentences.zh: 先王之制，大都不過三國之一，上下等差，各有定分，所以強幹弱枝，遏亂源而崇治本耳。

translations.literal: The former kings' system: a great commandery did not exceed one-third of the state; upper and lower grades of difference each had fixed allotments—this was to strengthen the trunk and weaken the branches, check the source of disorder, and honor the root of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Under the ancient system, even a great fief did not exceed one-third of the realm; each rank had its fixed allotment. That was how the center was strengthened and the periphery weakened, disorder was checked at its source, and governance was rooted in fundamentals.

sentences.zh: 今裂土分封，使諸王各有分地，蓋懲宋、元孤立，宗室不競之弊。

translations.literal: Today lands are split and enfeoffments made so that each prince has his allotted territory—this is roughly to take warning from the Song and Yuan isolation, when imperial clans did not contend.
translations.idiomatic: Today lands are divided and enfeoffed so that each prince holds his own territory—presumably to avoid the Song and Yuan mistake, when the imperial clan stood isolated and powerless.

sentences.zh: 而秦、晉、燕、齊、梁、楚、吳、蜀諸國，無不連邑數十。

translations.literal: Yet the states of Qin, Jin, Yan, Qi, Liang, Chu, Wu, and Shu each linked together dozens of districts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the princedoms of Qin, Jin, Yan, Qi, Liang, Chu, Wu, and Shu each controlled dozens of linked districts.

sentences.zh: 城郭宮室亞於天子之都，優之以甲兵衛士之盛。

translations.literal: Their walled cities and palaces were second only to the Son of Heaven's capital, and they were favored with abundant armored troops and guards.
translations.idiomatic: Their walled cities and palaces were second only to the imperial capital, and they were granted large forces of armored troops and guards.

sentences.zh: 臣恐數世之後，尾大不掉，然後削其地而奪之權，則必生觖望。

translations.literal: I fear that after several generations, when the tail grows too large to wag, and their lands are then cut back and their authority seized, discontent will surely arise.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that after several generations, when the branches have grown too heavy to control and the court tries to cut back their lands and strip their power, resentment will inevitably follow.

sentences.zh: 甚者緣間而起，防之無及矣。

translations.literal: In extreme cases they will rise on opportunity; one will be unable to guard against it in time.
translations.idiomatic: At worst they will seize their chance to rebel, and it will be too late to prevent disaster.

sentences.zh: 議者曰：『諸王皆天子骨肉，分地雖廣，立法雖侈，豈有抗衡之理？

translations.literal: Those who discuss the matter say: 'All the princes are the Son of Heaven's flesh and bone; though their allotments are broad and the statutes lavish, how could there be reason for them to contend against the throne?
translations.idiomatic: Some argue: 'The princes are all the emperor's own kin; though their domains are broad and their privileges lavish, how could they ever challenge the throne?

sentences.zh: 』臣竊以為不然。

translations.literal: ' I privately deem this not so.
translations.idiomatic: ' I respectfully disagree.

sentences.zh: 何不觀於漢、晉之事乎？

translations.literal: Why not look at the affairs of Han and Jin?
translations.idiomatic: Why not look at what happened under the Han and Jin dynasties?

sentences.zh: 孝景，高帝之孫也；

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaojing was Emperor Gaozu's grandson;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaojing was the grandson of Emperor Gaozu;

sentences.zh: 七國諸王，皆景帝之同祖父兄弟子孫也。

translations.literal: the kings of the Seven States were all Jing's cousins on their fathers' side, brothers, and their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: yet the kings of the Seven States were all Emperor Jing's paternal cousins, brothers, and their descendants.

sentences.zh: 一削其地，則遽構兵西向。

translations.literal: Once their lands were cut back, they at once mustered arms and turned west.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as their lands were reduced, they immediately raised armies and marched west.

sentences.zh: 晉之諸王，皆武帝親子孫也，易世之後，叠相攻伐，遂成劉、石之患。

translations.literal: The Jin princes were all Emperor Wu's own sons and descendants; after the change of reigns they attacked one another in succession, producing the calamity of the Liu and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin princes were all Emperor Wu's own sons and descendants; after the dynasty changed hands they fought one another in succession, bringing on the disaster of the Liu and Shi.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，分封逾制，禍患立生。

translations.literal: From this one may say: when enfeoffment exceeds the system, calamity is immediately born.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that when enfeoffment exceeds proper bounds, disaster follows at once.

sentences.zh: 援古證今，昭昭然矣。

translations.literal: Citing antiquity to prove the present—it is luminously clear.
translations.idiomatic: The lesson of history applied to the present could hardly be clearer.

sentences.zh: 此臣所以為太過者也。

translations.literal: This is why I deem enfeoffment excessive.
translations.idiomatic: This is why I consider enfeoffment one of the present excesses.

sentences.zh: 昔賈誼勸漢文帝，盡分諸國之地，空置之以待諸王子孫。

translations.literal: Formerly Jia Yi urged Emperor Wen of Han to divide entirely the lands of the princedoms, leaving them empty to await the sons and descendants of the princes.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Jia Yi urged Emperor Wen of Han to divide the princely domains completely, leaving vacant lands to be granted later to the princes' sons and descendants.

sentences.zh: 向使文帝早從誼言，則必無七國之禍。

translations.literal: If earlier Emperor Wen had followed Yi's words, then certainly there would have been no calamity of the Seven States.
translations.idiomatic: Had Emperor Wen followed Jia Yi's counsel in time, the calamity of the Seven States would never have occurred.

sentences.zh: 願及諸王未之國之先，節其都邑之制，減其衛兵，限其疆理，亦以待封諸王之子孫。

translations.literal: I pray that before the princes have gone to their states, the system governing their capitals be regulated, their guards reduced, their territorial boundaries limited—and that vacant lands likewise be held in reserve for the sons and descendants of the enfeoffed princes.
translations.idiomatic: I urge that before the princes depart for their domains, the scale of their capitals be restrained, their guards reduced, and their territories bounded—and that lands likewise be kept in reserve for the future enfeoffment of the princes' sons and descendants.

sentences.zh: 此制一定，然後諸王有賢且才者入為輔相，其余世為藩屏，與國同休。
