translations.literal: Once this system is fixed, then among the princes those who are worthy and talented may enter [court] as chief ministers; the rest may generation after generation serve as bulwarks of the realm, sharing fortune and misfortune with the state.
translations.idiomatic: Once this system is established, talented and worthy princes may enter court as chief ministers, while the rest serve generation after generation as bulwarks of the realm, sharing the state's fortune and fate.

sentences.zh: 割一時之恩，制萬世之利，消天變而安社稷，莫先於此。

translations.literal: To set aside momentary favor and establish benefit for ten thousand generations, to dispel heavenly anomalies and secure the altars of soil and grain—nothing comes before this.
translations.idiomatic: To forgo momentary indulgence and secure lasting benefit, to dispel heavenly portents and stabilize the altars of state—nothing should take precedence over this.

sentences.zh: 臣又觀歷代開國之君，未有不以任德結民心，以任刑失民心者。

translations.literal: I further observe that among founding sovereigns of successive dynasties, none failed to win the people's hearts through relying on virtue, nor to lose the people's hearts through relying on punishments.
translations.idiomatic: I further observe that among the founding sovereigns of successive dynasties, none who relied on virtue failed to win the people's hearts, and none who relied on punishments failed to lose them.

sentences.zh: 國祚長短，悉由於此。

translations.literal: Whether a dynasty's tenure is long or short—all depends on this.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a dynasty endures long or perishes soon depends entirely on this.

sentences.zh: 古者之斷死刑也，天子撤樂減膳，誠以天生斯民，立之司牲，固欲其並生，非欲其即死。

translations.literal: In antiquity when capital punishment was carried out, the Son of Heaven withdrew music and reduced his meals—for truly Heaven gave birth to these people and established overseers for them, intending that they all live together, not that they die at once.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when the death penalty was carried out, the Son of Heaven withdrew music and reduced his meals—for Heaven gave birth to the people and appointed rulers to shepherd them, truly intending that all should live, not that they should die.

sentences.zh: 不幸有不率教者入於其中，則不得已而授之以刑耳。

translations.literal: If unhappily there were those who did not follow instruction and fell among them, then there was no choice but to impose punishment upon them—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Only when, unhappily, someone failed to heed instruction and fell into wrongdoing was punishment imposed—there was no other choice.

sentences.zh: 議者曰：宋、元中葉，專事姑息，賞罰無章，以致亡滅。

translations.literal: Those who discuss the matter say: In the middle years of the Song and Yuan, they devoted themselves solely to indulgence; rewards and punishments lacked rule, leading to destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue: In the middle period of the Song and Yuan dynasties, rulers indulged wrongdoing without restraint, rewards and punishments were arbitrary, and the dynasties perished.

sentences.zh: 主上痛懲其弊，故制不宥之刑，權神變之法，使人知懼而莫測其端也。

translations.literal: Our sovereign, pained by these abuses, therefore instituted punishments without pardon and wielded laws of divine transformation, making people know fear yet unable to fathom their source.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, pained by these abuses, has therefore instituted punishments without pardon and wielded laws with discretionary severity, so that people live in fear yet cannot discern where punishment will strike.

sentences.zh: 臣又以為不然。

translations.literal: I again deem this not so.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully disagree.

sentences.zh: 開基之主垂範百世，一動一靜，必使子孫有所持守。

translations.literal: A founding sovereign sets an example for a hundred generations; in every movement and stillness he must enable his descendants to have something to uphold.
translations.idiomatic: A founding sovereign sets a precedent for a hundred generations; in every act and every restraint, he must give his descendants a standard to uphold.

sentences.zh: 況刑者，民之司命，可不慎歟！

translations.literal: Moreover, punishment is the arbiter of the people's lives—can one not be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: Punishment holds the people's lives in its hands—how can one not be cautious!

sentences.zh: 夫笞、杖、徒、流、死，今之五刑也。

translations.literal: Blows with the stick, beating with the rod, penal servitude, banishment, and death—these are the present five punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Blows with the light stick, blows with the heavy rod, penal servitude, exile, and death—these are the five punishments of today.

sentences.zh: 用此五刑，既無假貸，一出乎大公至正可也。

translations.literal: In applying these five punishments, since there is no leniency, it is enough that they proceed from utmost fairness and utmost rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: If these five punishments are applied without leniency, they need only proceed from utmost fairness and rectitude.

sentences.zh: 而用刑之際，多裁自聖衷，遂使治獄之吏務趨求意旨。

translations.literal: Yet in the application of punishments, many decisions come from the sacred heart, so that officials who handle cases strive to seek out the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in practice many punishments are decided by Your Majesty's personal judgment, so that judicial officials strive above all to discern the imperial intent.

sentences.zh: 深刻者多功，平反者得罪。

translations.literal: Those who are harsh and severe gain merit; those who overturn wrongful verdicts incur guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who impose harsh sentences win credit; those who overturn wrongful verdicts invite punishment.

sentences.zh: 欲求治獄之平，豈易得哉！

translations.literal: To seek fairness in the handling of cases—how can it be easily attained!
translations.idiomatic: Under such conditions, how can fair adjudication ever be achieved!

sentences.zh: 近者特旨，雜犯死罪，免死充軍。

translations.literal: Recently by special edict, for miscellaneous offenses carrying the death penalty, death was commuted to military exile.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, by special edict, those guilty of miscellaneous capital offenses have had death commuted to military exile.

sentences.zh: 又刪定舊律諸則，減宥有差矣。

translations.literal: The old statutes and their provisions were also revised and reduced, with pardons granted in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The old statutes have also been revised, with varying degrees of clemency introduced.

sentences.zh: 然未聞有戒敕治獄者務從平恕之條。

translations.literal: Yet I have not heard any admonition commanding those who handle cases to follow the principle of fairness and clemency.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have heard no admonition instructing judicial officials to adhere to fairness and clemency.

sentences.zh: 是以法司猶循故例。

translations.literal: Therefore the judicial offices still follow the old precedents.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, the judicial offices still follow the old precedents.

sentences.zh: 雖聞寬宥之名，未見寬宥之實。

translations.literal: Although one hears the name of leniency and pardon, one does not see the reality of leniency and pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Though the name of clemency is heard, the reality of clemency is not seen.

sentences.zh: 所謂實者，誠在主上，不在臣下也。

translations.literal: What is called the reality—truly it lies with the sovereign, not with his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The reality of clemency, I submit, depends on Your Majesty, not on your ministers.

sentences.zh: 故必有罪疑惟輕之意，而後好生之德洽於民心，此非可以淺淺期也。

translations.literal: Therefore there must be the intent that when guilt is doubtful, punish lightly—only then will the virtue of cherishing life permeate the people's hearts. This cannot be expected in shallow measure.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Your Majesty holds firmly to the principle that doubtful cases should be judged leniently will the virtue of cherishing life truly reach the people's hearts—and this cannot be achieved by superficial measures.

sentences.zh: 何以明其然也？

translations.literal: How may one make clear that this is so?
translations.idiomatic: How may this be demonstrated?

sentences.zh: 古之為士者，以登仕為榮，以罷職為辱。

translations.literal: Scholars of old took entering office as honor and dismissal from office as shame.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars of old took entering office as an honor and dismissal from office as a disgrace.

sentences.zh: 今之為士者，以混跡無聞為福，以受玷不錄為幸，以屯田工役為必獲之罪，以鞭笞捶楚為尋常之辱。

translations.literal: Scholars of today take blending in unnoticed as fortune, being tainted and not recorded as luck, agricultural colonization and corvée labor as punishments sure to be incurred, and flogging and beating as ordinary disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars of today count it a blessing to pass unnoticed, consider it fortunate to escape office with a blemished record, regard agricultural colonization and corvée labor as punishments sure to befall them, and treat flogging as an ordinary humiliation.

sentences.zh: 其始也，朝廷取天下之士，網羅捃摭，務無余逸。

translations.literal: At the outset, the court gathered scholars from throughout the realm, netting and collecting them, striving to leave none remaining.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, the court gathered scholars from across the realm, casting its net wide and leaving none behind.

sentences.zh: 有司敦迫上道，如捕重囚。

translations.literal: The responsible officials urgently pressed them onto the road, as if capturing serious criminals.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials pressed them onto the road as urgently as if pursuing felons.

sentences.zh: 比到京師，而除官多以貌選。

translations.literal: By the time they reached the capital, appointments were largely made by appearance.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached the capital, appointments were largely made on the basis of appearance.

sentences.zh: 所學或非其所用，所用或非其所學。

translations.literal: What they had studied was perhaps not what they were used for; what they were used for was perhaps not what they had studied.
translations.idiomatic: What they had studied was often not what they were assigned to do, and what they were assigned to do was often not what they had studied.

sentences.zh: 洎乎居官，一有差跌，茍免誅戮，則必在屯田工役之科。

translations.literal: Once in office, if there was any slip, and one barely escaped execution, one would surely fall under the category of agricultural colonization and corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, a single misstep—even if one escaped execution—would invariably mean assignment to agricultural colonization or corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 率是為常，不少顧惜，此豈陛下所樂為哉？

translations.literal: This became the constant rule, with little regard for sparing them—is this what Your Majesty takes pleasure in?
translations.idiomatic: This has become the norm, with little regard for mercy—is this truly what Your Majesty intends?

sentences.zh: 誠欲人之懼而不敢犯也。

translations.literal: Truly the intent is that people should fear and not dare to offend.
translations.idiomatic: The intent, to be sure, is that people should live in fear and not dare to offend.

sentences.zh: 竊見數年以來，誅殺亦可謂不少矣，而犯者相踵。

translations.literal: I privately observe that in recent years executions have been, one may say, not few, yet offenders follow one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that in recent years executions have been numerous, yet offenders continue in unbroken succession.

sentences.zh: 良由激勸不明，善惡無別。

translations.literal: Truly this is because encouragement and restraint are unclear, and good and evil are undistinguished.
translations.idiomatic: This is because incentives are unclear and good and evil are not distinguished.

sentences.zh: 議賢議能之法既廢，人不自勵，而為善者怠也。

translations.literal: Since the methods of recommending the worthy and the capable have been abandoned, people do not encourage themselves, and those who would do good grow slack.
translations.idiomatic: Since the practice of recommending the worthy and capable has been abandoned, people no longer strive to improve themselves, and those who would do good grow slack.

sentences.zh: 有人於此，廉如夷、齊，智如良、平，少戾於法。

translations.literal: Suppose there were someone here, as incorruptible as Boyi and Shuqi, as wise as Zhang Liang and Chen Ping, who slightly transgressed the law.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose there were someone as incorruptible as Boyi and Shuqi, as wise as Zhang Liang and Chen Ping, who committed a minor breach of the law.

sentences.zh: 上將錄長棄短而用之乎？

translations.literal: Would the sovereign record his strengths, set aside his weaknesses, and employ him?
translations.idiomatic: Would Your Majesty record his strengths, overlook his weaknesses, and employ him?

sentences.zh: 將舍其所長、苛其所短而置之法乎？

translations.literal: Or would he discard what he excels at, be harsh about his shortcomings, and subject him to the law?
translations.idiomatic: Or would Your Majesty discard his strengths, fix upon his shortcomings, and punish him according to the law?

sentences.zh: 茍取其長而舍其短，則中庸之材爭自奮於廉智。

translations.literal: If one takes his strengths and sets aside his weaknesses, then men of middling talent will all strive of themselves toward integrity and wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: If strengths are valued and weaknesses overlooked, men of ordinary talent will strive of their own accord toward integrity and wisdom.

sentences.zh: 倘苛其短而棄其長，則為善之人皆曰：某廉若是，某智若是，朝廷不少貸之，吾屬何所容其身乎！

translations.literal: If one is harsh about his weaknesses and discards his strengths, then those who would do good will all say: 'So-and-so was this incorruptible, so-and-so was this wise—yet the court showed him no leniency. Where can people like us find a place to stand!'
translations.idiomatic: But if shortcomings are seized upon and strengths discarded, those who would do good will say: 'So-and-so was this incorruptible, so-and-so was this wise—yet the court showed no leniency. Where can people like us find a place to stand!'

sentences.zh: 致使朝不謀夕，棄其廉恥，或事掊克，以備屯田工役之資者，率皆是也。

translations.literal: The result is that they do not plan beyond the morning for the evening, abandon their integrity and shame, or engage in extortion to prepare funds against agricultural colonization and corvée labor—such cases are mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: The result is that men live from day to day without plan, abandon their sense of honor, and resort to extortion to prepare against the threat of colonization and corvée labor—such cases are the rule.

sentences.zh: 若是非用刑之煩者乎？

translations.literal: Is this not the trouble of excessive use of punishments?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not the very trouble caused by excessive punishments?

sentences.zh: 漢嘗徙大族於山陵矣，未聞實之以罪人也。

translations.literal: The Han once relocated great clans to imperial tombs, yet I have never heard of filling them with criminals.
translations.idiomatic: The Han once relocated great clans to serve imperial tombs, but I have never heard of populating such places with criminals.

sentences.zh: 今鳳陽皇陵所在，龍興之地，而率以罪人居之，怨嗟愁苦之聲充斥園邑，殆非所以恭承宗廟意也。

translations.literal: Today at Fengyang, where the imperial tombs stand—the place where the dragon arose—criminals are generally made to dwell there; sounds of lamentation and bitter grief fill the park and town. This is scarcely the way to reverently inherit the intent of the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Today at Fengyang, where the imperial tombs stand—the very birthplace of the dynasty—criminals are sent to dwell in great numbers, and sounds of lamentation fill the region. This can scarcely accord with reverence for the imperial ancestors.

sentences.zh: 且夫強敵在前，則揚精鼓銳，攻之必克，擒之必獲，可也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when a powerful enemy stands before one, then to rouse the spirit and sharpen the edge, to attack and be sure to overcome, to capture and be sure to seize—this is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: When a powerful enemy stands before one, it is fitting to rouse the troops, attack with full force, and capture the foe.

sentences.zh: 今賊突竄山谷，以計求之，庶或可得。

translations.literal: Today bandits suddenly flee into mountain valleys; by stratagem one seeks them—perhaps they may be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Today the bandits have fled into the mountains; by careful strategy they may yet be taken.

sentences.zh: 顧勞重兵，彼方驚散，入不可蹤跡之地。

translations.literal: Yet if one exhausts heavy troops, they will only be startled and scattered, entering places where tracks cannot be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if heavy forces are deployed, the bandits will only scatter in alarm into terrain where no trail can be followed.

sentences.zh: 捕之數年，既無其方，而乃歸咎於新附戶籍之細民，而遷徙之。

translations.literal: After hunting them for several years without method, one then blames the common people of newly registered households and relocates them.
translations.idiomatic: After years of pursuit without success, blame is shifted to ordinary people of newly registered households, who are then forcibly relocated.

sentences.zh: 騷動數千里之地，室家不得休居，雞犬不得寧息。

translations.literal: Disturbance spreads across several thousand li; households cannot rest in peace, and fowl and dogs cannot know tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: Disturbance spreads across thousands of li; families cannot live in peace, and even fowl and dogs know no rest.

sentences.zh: 況新附之眾，向者流移他所，朝廷許其復業。

translations.literal: Moreover, among the newly attached populace, those who had previously drifted elsewhere were permitted by the court to resume their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, among the newly registered populace, those who had previously been displaced were permitted by the court to resume their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 今附籍矣，而又復遷徙，是法不信於民也。

translations.literal: Now that they are registered, they are again relocated—this means the law is not trusted by the people.
translations.idiomatic: Now that they have been registered, they are relocated again—thus the law loses the people's trust.

sentences.zh: 夫戶口盛而後田野辟，賦稅增。

translations.literal: When household registers flourish, then fields are opened and tax revenues increase.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the population grows are fields opened and tax revenues increased.

sentences.zh: 今責守令年增戶口，正為是也。

translations.literal: Today prefects and magistrates are charged with increasing household registers each year—precisely for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Today prefects and magistrates are charged with increasing the population each year—for precisely this reason.

sentences.zh: 近者已納稅糧之家，雖承旨分釋還家，而其心猶不自安。

translations.literal: Recently, households that had already paid their grain taxes, though released by imperial order to return home, still do not feel secure in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, households that had already paid their grain taxes, though released by imperial order to return home, still live in fear.

sentences.zh: 已起戶口，雖蒙憐恤，而猶見留開封祗候。

translations.literal: Those whose household registers have been drawn up, though shown compassion, are still detained at Kaifeng awaiting summons.
translations.idiomatic: Those whose names have been entered on the registers, though shown mercy, are still detained at Kaifeng awaiting further orders.

sentences.zh: 訛言驚動，不知所出。

translations.literal: False rumors stir alarm, and no one knows whence they come.
translations.idiomatic: False rumors spread alarm, and no one knows their source.

sentences.zh: 況太原諸郡，外界邊境，民心如此，甚非安邊之計也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the prefectures around Taiyuan border on the frontier; with the people's hearts in such a state, this is far from a plan to secure the border.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the prefectures around Taiyuan lie on the frontier; with popular sentiment in such a state, this is scarcely a policy for securing the border.

sentences.zh: 臣願自今朝廷宜存大體，赦小過。

translations.literal: I pray that from now on the court should preserve the larger principles and pardon minor faults.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that henceforth the court will uphold the larger principles of governance and pardon minor faults.

sentences.zh: 明詔天下，修舉「八議」之法，嚴禁深刻之吏。

translations.literal: Issue a clear edict to all under Heaven, restore the practice of the 'Eight Deliberations,' and strictly forbid harsh and severe officials.
translations.idiomatic: Issue a clear edict throughout the realm, restore the practice of the Eight Deliberations, and strictly forbid officials who impose harsh punishments.

sentences.zh: 斷獄平允者超遷之，殘酷裒斂者罷黜之。

translations.literal: Those who decide cases fairly and equitably should be promoted beyond their rank; those who are cruel and extortionate should be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who adjudicate fairly should be promoted; those who are cruel or extortionate should be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 鳳陽屯田之制，見在居屯者，聽其耕種起科。

translations.literal: As for the Fengyang agricultural colonization system, those presently dwelling in the colonies should be permitted to farm and begin paying taxes.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Fengyang colonization system, those presently settled in the colonies should be permitted to farm and begin paying taxes.

sentences.zh: 已起戶口、見留開封者，悉放復業。

translations.literal: Those whose household registers have been drawn up and who are detained at Kaifeng should all be released to resume their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Those whose names have been entered on the registers and who are detained at Kaifeng should all be released to resume their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 如此則足以隆好生之德，樹國祚長久之福。

translations.literal: In this way it would be enough to elevate the virtue of cherishing life and establish the blessing of a long-lasting dynastic tenure.
translations.idiomatic: In this way Your Majesty would elevate the virtue of cherishing life and secure the blessing of a long-lasting dynasty.

sentences.zh: 而兆民自安，天變自消矣。

translations.literal: Then the myriad people would be secure of themselves, and heavenly anomalies would dispel of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Then the myriad people would find peace of their own accord, and heavenly portents would subside.

sentences.zh: 昔者周自文、武至於成、康，而教化大行；

translations.literal: Formerly, from King Wen and King Wu of Zhou down to Kings Cheng and Kang, instruction and transformation were greatly carried out;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, from King Wen and King Wu of Zhou down to Kings Cheng and Kang, instruction and transformation flourished;

sentences.zh: 漢自高帝至於文、景，而始稱富庶。

translations.literal: from Emperor Gaozu of Han down to Emperors Wen and Jing, only then was the realm called prosperous and abundant.
translations.idiomatic: and from Emperor Gaozu of Han down to Emperors Wen and Jing, only then did the realm become truly prosperous.

sentences.zh: 蓋天下之治亂，氣化之轉移，人心之趨向，非一朝一夕故也。

translations.literal: For the order and disorder of all under Heaven, the shifting of cosmic influence, and the direction of people's hearts are not matters of a single morning or evening.
translations.idiomatic: For the order and disorder of the realm, the shifting of cosmic influence, and the direction of popular sentiment are not achieved in a day.

sentences.zh: 今國家紀元，九年於茲，偃兵息民，天下大定。

translations.literal: Today the state has counted its years of rule—nine years have passed; arms are stilled and the people rest; all under Heaven is greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: Nine years have now passed since the founding of the dynasty; arms have been stilled, the people have rested, and the realm is largely at peace.

sentences.zh: 紀綱大正，法令修明，可謂治矣。

translations.literal: The fundamental principles are greatly rectified, laws and edicts are well ordered and clear—one may say there is order.
translations.idiomatic: Fundamental institutions have been rectified and laws made clear—the realm may already be called well governed.

sentences.zh: 而陛下切切以民俗澆漓，人不知懼，法出而奸生，令下而詐起。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty urgently concerns himself that popular custom is thin and dissolute, people do not know fear, when laws issue wickedness arises, and when orders descend deceit springs up.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty urgently concerns himself that popular custom has grown dissolute, that people no longer know fear, that laws breed wickedness as soon as they are issued, and that deceit springs up as soon as orders are given.

sentences.zh: 故或朝信而幕猜者有之；

translations.literal: Therefore there are those trusted in the morning yet suspected by evening;
translations.idiomatic: Thus some are trusted in the morning yet suspected by evening;

sentences.zh: 昨日所進，今日被戮者有之。

translations.literal: those promoted yesterday, executed today.
translations.idiomatic: some promoted yesterday are executed today.

sentences.zh: 乃至令下而尋改，已赦而復收。

translations.literal: It reaches the point that orders are issued and soon changed, pardons granted and then revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Orders are issued and soon reversed; pardons are granted and then withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 天下臣民莫之適從。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm, ministers and people have nothing by which to guide themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the realm, officials and common people alike no longer know how to conduct themselves.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂天下之趨於治，猶堅冰之泮也。

translations.literal: I, in my foolishness, say that the realm's movement toward order is like the melting of hard ice.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly submit that the realm's movement toward order is like the melting of hard ice.

sentences.zh: 冰之泮，非太陽所能驟致。

translations.literal: The melting of ice is not something the sun can suddenly bring about.
translations.idiomatic: Ice does not melt all at once, even under the full force of the sun.

sentences.zh: 陽氣發生，土脈微動，然後得以融釋。

translations.literal: Yang energy arises, the earth's veins stir slightly—only then can melting and release be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Yang energy must arise, the earth's veins must stir slightly—only then does melting begin.

sentences.zh: 聖人之治天下，亦猶是也。

translations.literal: The sage's governance of all under Heaven is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The governance of a sage over the realm is the same.

sentences.zh: 刑以威之，禮以導之，漸民以仁，摩民以義，而後其化熙熙。

translations.literal: Punishment to awe them, rites to guide them, gradually imbuing the people with benevolence, polishing the people with righteousness—only then does transformation become flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment to inspire awe, rites to guide conduct, gradually imbuing the people with benevolence and refining them with righteousness—only then does transformation flourish.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「如有王者，必世而後仁。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "If there were one who would become king, it would take a generation before benevolence prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "If there were one who would become king, it would take a generation before benevolence prevailed.

sentences.zh: 」此非空言也。

translations.literal: " This is not empty speech.
translations.idiomatic: " This is no empty saying.

sentences.zh: 求治之道，莫先於正風俗；

translations.literal: In the way of seeking order, nothing comes before rectifying popular custom;
translations.idiomatic: In the pursuit of good governance, nothing comes before rectifying popular custom;

sentences.zh: 正風俗之道，莫先於守令知所務；

translations.literal: in the way of rectifying popular custom, nothing comes before prefects and magistrates knowing what they should devote themselves to;
translations.idiomatic: and in rectifying popular custom, nothing comes before prefects and magistrates knowing their proper duties;

sentences.zh: 使守令知所務，莫先於風憲知所重；

translations.literal: to make prefects and magistrates know what they should devote themselves to, nothing comes before censorial officials knowing what to emphasize;
translations.idiomatic: to ensure that prefects and magistrates know their duties, nothing comes before censorial officials knowing what to emphasize;

sentences.zh: 使風憲知所重，莫先於朝廷知所尚。

translations.literal: to make censorial officials know what to emphasize, nothing comes before the court knowing what to esteem.
translations.idiomatic: and to ensure that censorial officials know what to emphasize, nothing comes before the court knowing what to esteem.

sentences.zh: 古郡守、縣令，以正率下，以善導民，使化成俗美。

translations.literal: The prefects and magistrates of old led those below through rectitude and guided the people through goodness, making instruction transform and custom beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates of old led by example and guided the people toward goodness, so that instruction transformed society and custom became refined.

sentences.zh: 征賦、期會、獄訟、簿書，固其末也。

translations.literal: Tax collection, scheduled assemblies, lawsuits, and ledger documents—these were truly the lesser matters.
translations.idiomatic: Tax collection, scheduled reports, lawsuits, and ledger keeping were truly secondary matters.

sentences.zh: 今之守令以戶口、錢糧、獄論為急務；

translations.literal: Today's prefects and magistrates take household registers, grain taxes, and criminal cases as urgent tasks;
translations.idiomatic: Today's prefects and magistrates treat household registers, grain taxes, and criminal cases as their urgent priorities;

sentences.zh: 至於農桑、學校，王政之本，乃視為虛文而置之，將何。

translations.literal: As for agriculture and sericulture, and schools—the roots of royal governance—they are regarded as empty form and set aside—how then
translations.idiomatic: yet agriculture, sericulture, and schools—the foundations of royal governance—are treated as empty formalities and set aside. How then

sentences.zh: 以教養斯民哉？

translations.literal: to educate and nurture these people?
translations.idiomatic: are the people to be educated and nurtured?

sentences.zh: 以農桑言之：方春州縣下一白帖，裏甲回申文狀而已，守令未嘗親視種藝次第、旱澇戒備之道也。

translations.literal: Speaking of agriculture and sericulture: at the start of spring the prefecture and district issue a white notice, the li-jia head returns a written report—that is all. Prefects and magistrates have never personally inspected the sequence of planting, or the methods of guarding against drought and flood.
translations.idiomatic: Take agriculture and sericulture: at the start of spring the prefecture and district issue a white notice, the li-jia head submits a written report—and that is all. Prefects and magistrates never personally inspect planting schedules or preparations against drought and flood.

sentences.zh: 以學校言之：廩膳諸生，國家資之以取人才之地也。

translations.literal: Speaking of schools: the stipended students are the place where the state relies to obtain talented men.
translations.idiomatic: Take schools: the stipended students are the state's means of cultivating talent.

sentences.zh: 今四方師生，缺員甚多。

translations.literal: Today teachers and students throughout the four directions have many vacant places.
translations.idiomatic: Today schools throughout the realm have many vacant places.

sentences.zh: 縱使具員，守令亦鮮有以禮讓之實作其成器者。

translations.literal: Even if all places were filled, prefects and magistrates would rarely, through the reality of courtesy and deference, make them into finished vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Even when fully staffed, prefects and magistrates rarely cultivate students through genuine instruction in courtesy and deference.

sentences.zh: 朝廷切切於社學，屢行取勘師生姓名、所習課業。

translations.literal: The court urgently concerns itself with community schools, repeatedly conducting inspections to verify teachers' and students' names and the subjects they study.
translations.idiomatic: The court urgently concerns itself with community schools, repeatedly ordering inspections of teachers' and students' names and their course of study.

sentences.zh: 乃今社鎮城郭，或但置立門牌，遠村僻處則又徒存其名，守令不過具文案、備照刷而已。

translations.literal: Yet today in market towns and walled cities, some merely set up name plaques; in distant villages and secluded places the names alone remain. Prefects and magistrates do no more than prepare documents and ready checklists for inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Yet today in market towns and cities, some schools exist only as name plaques on doorways; in remote villages the name alone survives. Prefects and magistrates do no more than prepare documents and checklists for inspection.

sentences.zh: 上官分部按臨，亦但循習故常，依紙上照刷，未嘗巡行點視也。

translations.literal: Superior officials on circuit inspection likewise merely follow old custom, relying on paper checklists, and have never toured to inspect in person.
translations.idiomatic: Superior officials on circuit inspection likewise follow old custom, relying on paper checklists, and never tour the schools to inspect them in person.

sentences.zh: 興廢之實，上下視為虛文。

translations.literal: The reality of establishing and abolishing [schools], above and below regard as empty form.
translations.idiomatic: The substance of what was established or allowed to lapse is treated throughout the bureaucracy as mere empty form.

sentences.zh: 小民不知孝弟忠信為何物，而禮義廉恥掃地矣。

translations.literal: Common people do not know what filial piety, fraternal duty, loyalty, and good faith are; ritual, righteousness, integrity, and shame have been swept to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The common people no longer know what filial piety, brotherly duty, loyalty, and good faith mean—and propriety, righteousness, integrity, and a sense of shame have been utterly cast aside.

sentences.zh: 風紀之司，所以代朝廷宣導德化，訪察善惡。

translations.literal: The offices of local discipline exist to represent the court in proclaiming and guiding moral transformation, and in investigating good and evil.
translations.idiomatic: The censorial apparatus exists to represent the court in spreading moral instruction and investigating right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 聽訟讞獄，其一事耳。

translations.literal: Hearing lawsuits and judging cases is but one matter among them.
translations.idiomatic: Adjudicating lawsuits and passing judgment on cases is only one of its duties.

sentences.zh: 今專以獄訟為要。

translations.literal: Now they concentrate solely on lawsuits as the essential task.
translations.idiomatic: Today they treat criminal cases as the only priority.

sentences.zh: 忠臣、孝子、義夫、節婦，視為末節而不暇舉，所謂宣導風化者安在哉？

translations.literal: Loyal ministers, filial sons, righteous husbands, and chaste women are regarded as trivial matters with no time to recommend them—where is the so-called spreading of custom and transformation?
translations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers, filial sons, righteous husbands, and chaste wives are dismissed as minor matters, with no time to commend them—where, then, is this "moral instruction" they speak of?

sentences.zh: 其始但知以去一贓吏、決一獄訟為治，而不知勸民成俗，使民遷善遠罪，乃治之大者。

translations.literal: At the outset they know only to regard removing one corrupt official and deciding one lawsuit as governance, and do not know that encouraging the people to form custom and causing the people to turn toward goodness and away from crime is the greater part of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Officials begin by thinking that removing a corrupt magistrate or clearing a court case counts as governing well, never grasping that the greater task is to guide the people toward custom, turning them toward virtue and away from crime.

sentences.zh: 此守令風憲未審輕重之失也。

translations.literal: This is the failure of prefects, magistrates, and censorial officials to discern what is weighty and what is light.
translations.idiomatic: This is the error of prefects, magistrates, and censorial officials who fail to distinguish the weighty from the trivial.

sentences.zh: 《王制》論鄉秀士升於司徒曰「選士」，司徒論其秀士而升於太學曰「俊士」，大樂正又論造士之秀升之司馬曰「進士」，司馬辨論官材，論定，然後官之；

translations.literal: In the 《Royal Regulations》, when discussing village outstanding scholars promoted to the Minister of Education, they are called "selected scholars"; the Minister of Education evaluates outstanding scholars and promotes them to the Imperial Academy as "eminent scholars"; the Grand Music Master further evaluates outstanding cultivated scholars and promotes them to the Minister of War as "presented scholars"; the Minister of War discusses and distinguishes official talent, and when the evaluation is settled, only then appoints them to office;
translations.idiomatic: In the 《Royal Regulations》, village scholars of distinction promoted to the Minister of Education were called "selected scholars." Those the Minister judged outstanding and sent upward to the Imperial Academy were called "eminent scholars." The Grand Music Master, evaluating the finest cultivated scholars, advanced them to the Minister of War as "presented scholars." The Minister of War weighed each man's fitness for office, and only after judgment was complete were men appointed.

sentences.zh: 任官，然後爵之。

translations.literal: After appointing to office, only then ennobling them.
translations.idiomatic: Only after they had served in office were they ennobled.

sentences.zh: 其考之之詳若此，故成周得人為盛。

translations.literal: Their examination was so thorough as this; therefore the Zhou at its completion excelled in obtaining men.
translations.idiomatic: The scrutiny was this thorough—which is why the Zhou at its height drew so many able men.

sentences.zh: 今使天下諸生考於禮部，升於太學，歷練眾職，任之以事，可以洗歷代舉選之陋，上法成周。

translations.literal: Now if scholars throughout the realm are examined by the Ministry of Rites, promoted to the Imperial Academy, trained through various offices, and entrusted with duties, this can wash away the defects of selection through the ages and model the Zhou at its completion above.
translations.idiomatic: The present system—students examined by the Ministry of Rites, promoted to the Imperial Academy, rotated through various posts, and entrusted with responsibility—could cleanse the abuses of centuries of recruitment and restore the Zhou model.

sentences.zh: 然而升於太學者，或未數月，遽選入官，間或委以民社。

translations.literal: However, those promoted to the Imperial Academy sometimes, before even several months have passed, are suddenly selected for office, and occasionally entrusted with the people's altars.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those admitted to the Imperial Academy are sometimes selected for office within a few months—and sometimes entrusted straightaway with a magistracy.

sentences.zh: 臣恐其人未諳時務，未熟朝廷禮法，不能宣導德化，上乖國政，而下困黎民也。

translations.literal: I fear such persons have not yet mastered current affairs, are not yet familiar with court ritual and law, cannot proclaim and guide moral transformation, and will deviate from national policy above while distressing the common people below.
translations.idiomatic: I fear these men do not yet understand affairs of the day, are unfamiliar with court ritual and law, and cannot spread moral instruction—serving the state's policies ill above while burdening the people below.

sentences.zh: 開國以來，選舉秀才不為不多，所任名位不為不重，自今數之，在者有幾？

translations.literal: Since the founding of the state, the selection of xiucai has not been few, and the offices and ranks entrusted to them not unimportant—counting from today, how many remain?
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding, no small number of xiucai have been selected and given weighty posts—yet counting those who remain today, how many are there?

sentences.zh: 臣恐後之視今，亦猶今之視昔。

translations.literal: I fear that those who come after will view the present as the present views the past.
translations.idiomatic: I fear posterity will look upon our day as we now look upon earlier times.

sentences.zh: 昔年所舉之人，豈不深可痛惜乎！

translations.literal: Those raised up in former years—are they not deeply worthy of grief and regret?
translations.idiomatic: Those men elevated in years past—is their loss not cause for deep sorrow?

sentences.zh: 凡此皆臣所為求治太速之過也。

translations.literal: All this is the fault I assign to seeking order too hastily.
translations.idiomatic: All of this, I submit, stems from the error of pursuing order too hastily.

sentences.zh: 昔者宋有天下蓋三百余年。

translations.literal: Formerly the Song held the realm for roughly more than three hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: The Song once held the realm for some three hundred years.

sentences.zh: 其始，以禮義教其民，當其盛時，閭閻裏巷皆有忠厚之風，至於恥言人之過失。

translations.literal: At the beginning they taught their people with ritual and righteousness; at its height, every lane and alleyway bore an atmosphere of sincerity and kindness, to the point that people were ashamed to speak of others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: At its beginning the dynasty taught its people ritual and righteousness. At its height, lanes and alleys everywhere breathed sincerity and good faith, and men were ashamed to speak of another's failings.

sentences.zh: 洎乎末年，忠臣義士視死如歸，婦人女子羞被汙辱，此皆教化之效也。

translations.literal: By its final years, loyal ministers and righteous men viewed death as returning home; women and girls were shamed by defilement—all this was the effect of instruction and transformation.
translations.idiomatic: By its end loyal ministers and righteous men went to their deaths as though returning home, and women and girls chose death before dishonor. All this was the fruit of moral instruction.

sentences.zh: 元之有國，其本不立，犯禮義之分，壞廉恥之防。

translations.literal: When the Yuan held the state, its root was not established; it violated the bounds of ritual and righteousness and broke down the defenses of integrity and shame.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan's foundation was never secure: it transgressed the bounds of ritual and righteousness and tore down the bulwarks of integrity and shame.

sentences.zh: 不數十年，棄城降敵者不可勝數，雖老儒碩臣甘心屈辱。

translations.literal: Within not several decades, those who abandoned cities and surrendered to the enemy were beyond counting—even aged Confucian scholars and eminent ministers willingly submitted to humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few decades, countless men surrendered their cities and submitted to the enemy—even venerable Confucian scholars and senior ministers accepted humiliation without protest.

sentences.zh: 此禮義廉恥不振之弊。

translations.literal: This is the harm of ritual, righteousness, integrity, and shame not being roused.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the consequences when ritual, righteousness, integrity, and shame no longer stir the heart.

sentences.zh: 遺風流俗至今未革，深可怪也。

translations.literal: Surviving customs and flowing habits to this day have not been reformed—a thing deeply strange.
translations.idiomatic: Those surviving customs endure to this day unchanged—a thing deeply troubling.

sentences.zh: 臣謂：莫若敦仁義，尚廉恥。

translations.literal: Your servant submits: nothing is better than honoring benevolence and righteousness and elevating integrity and shame.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that nothing would serve better than to champion benevolence and righteousness and hold integrity and shame in high regard.

sentences.zh: 守令則責其以農桑、學校為急，風憲則責其先教化、審法律，以平獄緩刑為急。

translations.literal: For prefects and magistrates, hold them responsible to treat agriculture and sericulture and schools as urgent; for censorial officials, hold them responsible to put instruction first, examine the laws carefully, and treat fair judgment and lenient punishment as urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates should be held responsible for giving agriculture, sericulture, and schools first priority; censorial officials should be charged to put moral instruction first, review the laws carefully, and treat equitable judgment and lenient punishments as urgent.

sentences.zh: 如此，則德澤下流，求治之道庶幾得矣。

translations.literal: If this is done, then virtuous influence will flow downward and the way of seeking order will perhaps be attained.
translations.idiomatic: Thus would benevolent influence flow downward, and the path toward order might nearly be found.

sentences.zh: 郡邑諸生升於太學者，須令在學肄業，或三年，或五年，精通一經，兼習一藝，然後入選。

translations.literal: Students from commanderies and districts promoted to the Imperial Academy must be required to study in the academy, for either three or five years, mastering one classic and also learning one skill—only then may they enter selection.
translations.idiomatic: Students from the provinces promoted to the Imperial Academy should be required to remain and study for three or five years, mastering one classic and one practical skill before they become eligible for selection.

sentences.zh: 或宿衛，或辦事，以觀公卿大夫之能，而後任之以政，則其學識兼懋，庶無敗事。

translations.literal: Whether serving in palace guard or handling business, so as to observe the capabilities of ministers and grandees—only then entrust them with government; then their learning and competence would both flourish, and failures might be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: They should serve as guards or handle administrative duties so that the abilities of senior officials can be observed—and only thereafter be entrusted with governance. Then learning and competence would flourish together, and misrule might be avoided.

sentences.zh: 且使知祿位皆天之祿位，而可以塞凱覦之心也。

translations.literal: Moreover, this would make them know that salary and rank are Heaven's salary and rank, and thus could block hearts that covet and look on with envy.
translations.idiomatic: It would also teach them that rank and emolument are gifts of Heaven, and so check the covetous heart.

sentences.zh: 治道既得，陛下端拱穆清，待以歲月，則陰陽調而風雨時，諸福吉祥莫不畢至。

translations.literal: Once the way of governance is attained, Your Majesty sitting upright in dignity and repose, waiting through the months and years—then yin and yang will harmonize and wind and rain come seasonally; every blessing and auspicious sign will all arrive in full.
translations.idiomatic: Once governance is rightly established, Your Majesty may sit in dignified ease and wait through the years—then yin and yang will balance, winds and rains arrive in season, and every blessing and omen will follow in turn.

sentences.zh: 尚何天變之不消哉？

translations.literal: Why then would celestial anomalies not be dispelled?
translations.idiomatic: What celestial portent would then fail to pass away?

sentences.zh: 書上，帝大怒曰：「小子間吾骨肉，速逮來，吾手射之！

translations.literal: When the letter was submitted, the Emperor raged: "This stripling is sowing discord among my flesh and blood—seize him at once! I will shoot him with my own hand!
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor flew into a rage: "This stripling is sowing discord among my flesh and blood—seize him at once! I will shoot him with my own hand!

sentences.zh: 」既至，丞相乘帝喜以奏，下刑部獄。

translations.literal: " When he arrived, the chief councillor waited until the Emperor was pleased and then presented the matter; he was sent down to the Ministry of Justice prison.
translations.idiomatic: " When he arrived, the chief councillor waited until the Emperor was in good humor and then reported the case; Boju was sent to the Ministry of Justice prison.

sentences.zh: 死獄中。

translations.literal: He died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: He died in prison.

sentences.zh: 先是，伯巨將上書，語其友曰：「今天下惟三事可患耳，其二事易見而患遲，其一事難見而患速。

translations.literal: Earlier, before submitting his letter, Boju told his friend: "Today only three things in the realm are to be feared; two are easy to see though the harm is slow, one is hard to see though the harm is swift.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, before submitting his memorial, Boju told a friend: "Today only three things in the realm are to be feared. Two are easy to see, though the harm they bring is slow; one is hard to see, though the harm it brings is swift.

sentences.zh: 縱無明詔，吾猶將言之，況求言乎。

translations.literal: Even without a clear edict I would still speak; how much more when counsel is sought?
translations.idiomatic: Even without a clear edict I would still speak—how much more when counsel is sought?

sentences.zh: 」其意蓋謂分封也。

translations.literal: " His meaning was presumably enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: " His meaning was presumably enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 然是時諸王止建藩號，未曾裂土，不盡如伯巨所言。

translations.literal: Yet at that time the princes had only established their fief titles and had not yet had lands split off—not entirely as Boju described.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at that time the princes had only received their fief titles and had not yet been granted separate territories—not entirely as Boju had described.

sentences.zh: 迨洪武末年，燕王屢奉命出塞，勢始強。

translations.literal: By the late Hongwu period the Prince of Yan repeatedly received orders to campaign beyond the frontier, and his power began to grow strong.
translations.idiomatic: By the late Hongwu reign the Prince of Yan repeatedly received orders to campaign beyond the frontier, and his power began to grow.

sentences.zh: 後因削奪稱兵，遂有天下，人乃以伯巨為先見雲。

translations.literal: Later, because of territorial reductions he took up arms, seized the realm, and people then regarded Boju as having foreseen it first.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after his fiefs were stripped away, he took up arms and seized the realm—and people then regarded Boju as having foreseen it.

sentences.zh: 鄭士利，字好義，寧海人。

translations.literal: Zheng Shili, courtesy name Haoyi, was a native of Ninghai.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shili, styled Haoyi, was a native of Ninghai.

sentences.zh: 兄士元，剛直有才學，由進士歷官湖廣按察使僉事。

translations.literal: His elder brother Shiyuan was upright and had talent and learning; as a jinshi he served successively as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Shiyuan was upright and talented; as a jinshi he rose to serve as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 荊、襄卒乘亂掠婦女，吏不敢問，士元立言於將領，還所掠。

translations.literal: Soldiers in Jing and Xiang took advantage of disorder to seize women; officials dared not inquire. Shiyuan spoke directly to the commanders, and the seized women were returned.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers in Jing and Xiang took advantage of the disorder to seize women; officials dared not intervene. Shiyuan spoke directly to the commanders, and the seized women were returned.

sentences.zh: 安陸有冤獄，御史臺已讞上，士元奏其冤，得白。

translations.literal: In Anlu there was a wrongful case; the Censorate had already submitted its verdict. Shiyuan memorialized the injustice, and the case was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: In Anlu there was a wrongful conviction; the Censorate had already submitted its verdict. Shiyuan memorialized the injustice, and the accused was cleared.

sentences.zh: 會考校錢谷冊書，空印事覺。

translations.literal: It happened that during an audit of grain-and-revenue account books, the blank-seal affair came to light.
translations.idiomatic: During an audit of grain-and-revenue account books, the blank-seal affair came to light.

sentences.zh: 凡主印者論死，佐貳以下榜一百，戍遠方。

translations.literal: All seal-holders were sentenced to death; assistants and deputies were flogged one hundred strokes and sent to garrison distant regions.
translations.idiomatic: All seal-holders were sentenced to death; assistants and deputies were flogged one hundred strokes and exiled to distant garrisons.

sentences.zh: 士元亦坐是系獄。

translations.literal: Shiyuan was also implicated and imprisoned for this.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyuan was also implicated and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 時帝方盛怒，以為欺罔，丞相御史莫敢諫。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor was in a great rage, believing he had been deceived; the chief councillor and censors dared not remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was then in a towering rage, believing he had been deceived; the chief councillor and censors dared not remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 士利嘆曰：「上不知，以空印為大罪。

translations.literal: Shili sighed: "The Emperor does not understand—he treats blank seals as a great crime.
translations.idiomatic: Shili sighed: "The Emperor does not understand—he treats blank seals as a grave crime.

sentences.zh: 誠得人言之，上聖明，寧有不悟？

translations.literal: If only someone would speak of it to him—His Majesty is wise; how could he fail to see?
translations.idiomatic: If only someone would speak to him—His Majesty is wise; how could he fail to understand?

sentences.zh: 」會星變求言。

translations.literal: " Just then a stellar anomaly prompted a call for counsel.
translations.idiomatic: " Just then a stellar anomaly prompted a call for counsel.

sentences.zh: 士利曰：「可矣。

translations.literal: Shili said: "The time has come.
translations.idiomatic: Shili said: "The time has come.

sentences.zh: 」既而讀詔：「有假公言私者，罪。

translations.literal: " But then reading the edict: "Whoever uses public speech for private ends will be punished.
translations.idiomatic: " But then he read the edict: "Whoever uses public speech for private ends will be punished.

sentences.zh: 」士利曰：「吾所欲言，為天子殺無罪者耳。

translations.literal: " Shili said: "What I wish to say is that the Son of Heaven is killing the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: " Shili said: "What I wish to say is that the Son of Heaven is killing the innocent.

sentences.zh: 吾兄非主印者，固當出。

translations.literal: My brother was not the seal-holder; he should have been released anyway.
translations.idiomatic: My brother was not the seal-holder; he should have been released in any case.

sentences.zh: 需吾兄杖出乃言，即死不恨。」

translations.literal: Wait until my brother has been flogged and released, and then I will speak—even if I die, I will not regret it."
translations.idiomatic: I will wait until my brother has been flogged and released, and then I will speak—even if I die, I will not regret it."

sentences.zh: 士元出，士利乃為書數千言，言數事，而於空印事尤詳。

translations.literal: After Shiyuan was released, Shili composed a letter of several thousand characters on several matters, treating the blank-seal affair with especial detail.
translations.idiomatic: After Shiyuan was released, Shili composed a memorial of several thousand characters on several matters, treating the blank-seal affair with especial detail.

sentences.zh: 曰：「陛下欲深罪空印者，恐奸吏得挾空印紙，為文移以虐民耳。

translations.literal: He wrote: "Your Majesty wishes to punish blank-seal offenders severely, fearing that corrupt officials might grasp blank sealed paper to draft documents and oppress the people.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Your Majesty wishes to punish blank-seal offenders severely, fearing that corrupt officials might seize blank sealed paper to draft documents and oppress the people.

sentences.zh: 夫文移必完印乃可。

translations.literal: Official documents must have complete seals before they can be used.
translations.idiomatic: Official documents require a complete seal before they can be used.

sentences.zh: 今考較書策，乃合兩縫印，非一印一紙比。

translations.literal: Today's audit account books join two seam-seals—they are not one seal to one sheet.
translations.idiomatic: The account books used in audits bear seals across both margins of the binding—they are not one seal to one sheet.

sentences.zh: 縱得之，亦不能行，況不可得乎？

translations.literal: Even if one obtained them, they could not be used—how much less could they be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Even if one obtained them, they could not be used—how much less could they be obtained at all?

sentences.zh: 錢谷之數，府必合省，省必合部，數難懸決，至部乃定。

translations.literal: Figures for revenue and grain must be consolidated by the prefecture with the province and by the province with the ministry; numbers can hardly be decided in advance—they are fixed only when they reach the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue and grain figures must be consolidated by the prefecture with the province and by the province with the ministry; the totals can hardly be decided in advance—they are fixed only when they reach the ministry.

sentences.zh: 省府去部遠者六七千里，近亦三四千里，冊成而後用印，往返非期年不可。

translations.literal: From province and prefecture to the ministry is six or seven thousand li at farthest, and three or four thousand at nearest; the register must be completed before seals are applied, and a round trip cannot be done in less than a full year.
translations.idiomatic: From province and prefecture to the ministry is six or seven thousand li at farthest and three or four thousand at nearest; the register must be completed before seals are applied, and a round trip cannot be completed in less than a full year.

sentences.zh: 以故先印而後書。

translations.literal: For this reason seals are applied first and writing comes after.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason seals were applied first and the text written afterward.

sentences.zh: 此權宜之務，所從來久，何足深罪？

translations.literal: This is an expedient of long standing—why should it be treated as a grave crime?
translations.idiomatic: This expedient has been in use for a long time—why should it be treated as a grave crime?

sentences.zh: 且國家立法，必先明示天下而後罪犯法者，以其故犯也。

translations.literal: Moreover when the state establishes law, it must first make it clear to the realm before punishing those who violate the law—for their violation was knowing.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the state establishes law, it must first make it clear to the realm before punishing violators—for only then is the violation knowing.

sentences.zh: 自立國至今，未嘗有空印之律。

translations.literal: From the founding of the state until now there has never been a law on blank seals.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding of the state until now there has never been a law against blank seals.

sentences.zh: 有司相承，不知其罪。

translations.literal: Officials passed it down through generations without knowing it was a crime.
translations.idiomatic: Officials passed the practice down through generations without knowing it was a crime.

sentences.zh: 今一旦誅之，何以使受誅者無詞？

translations.literal: Now to execute them all at once—how can those executed be left without argument?
translations.idiomatic: Now to execute them all at once—how can those put to death be left without a word in their own defense?

sentences.zh: 朝廷求賢士，置庶位，得之甚難。

translations.literal: The court seeks worthy men and fills numerous offices—obtaining them is very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The court seeks worthy men and fills numerous offices—finding them is very difficult.

sentences.zh: 位至郡守，皆數十年所成就。

translations.literal: Reaching the rank of prefect takes decades of achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the rank of prefect takes decades of achievement.

sentences.zh: 通達廉明之士，非如草菅然，可刈而復生也。

translations.literal: Clear-sighted, incorrupt officials are not like grass that can be cut and grow again.
translations.idiomatic: Clear-sighted, incorrupt officials are not like grass that can be cut down and grow again.

sentences.zh: 陛下奈何以不足罪之罪，而壞足用之材乎？

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty, for a crime insufficient to warrant death, destroy men fully fit for use?
translations.idiomatic: How can Your Majesty, for a crime insufficient to warrant death, destroy men fully fit to serve?

sentences.zh: 臣竊為陛下惜之。

translations.literal: Your servant privately grieves this for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I grieve this for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」書成，閉門逆旅泣數日。

translations.literal: " When the letter was finished, he closed his door at his inn and wept for several days.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was finished, he shut himself in at his inn and wept for several days.

sentences.zh: 兄子問曰：「叔何所苦？

translations.literal: His nephew asked: "Uncle, what troubles you?
translations.idiomatic: His nephew asked: "Uncle, what troubles you?

sentences.zh: 」士利曰：「吾有書欲上，觸天子怒，必受禍。

translations.literal: " Shili said: "I have a letter I wish to submit; it will provoke the Son of Heaven's anger—I am sure to suffer harm.
translations.idiomatic: " Shili said: "I have a memorial I wish to submit; it will provoke the Son of Heaven's anger—I am sure to suffer for it.

sentences.zh: 然殺我，生數百人，我何所恨！

translations.literal: Yet if killing me saves several hundred lives, what have I to regret!
translations.idiomatic: Yet if killing me saves several hundred lives, what have I to regret!

sentences.zh: 」遂入奏。

translations.literal: " He then entered and submitted the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " He then entered court and submitted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝覽書，大怒，下丞相御史雜問，究使者。

translations.literal: The Emperor read the letter and flew into a rage; he handed the case to the chief councillor and censors for joint interrogation, demanding to find who had sent the messenger.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor read the memorial and flew into a rage; he handed the case to the chief councillor and censors for joint interrogation, demanding to find who had sent it.

sentences.zh: 士利笑曰：「顧吾書足用否耳。

translations.literal: Shili laughed: "I care only whether my letter served its purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Shili laughed: "I care only whether my memorial served its purpose.

sentences.zh: 吾業為國家言事，自分必死，誰為我謀？

translations.literal: I spoke for the state, knowing I must die—who would scheme for me?
translations.idiomatic: I spoke for the state, knowing I must die—who would scheme on my behalf?

sentences.zh: 」獄具，與士元皆輸作江浦，而空印者竟多不免。

translations.literal: " When the case was closed, both he and Shiyuan were sent to labor at Jiangpu, yet most of the blank-seal offenders ultimately could not escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " When the case was closed, both he and Shiyuan were sent to labor at Jiangpu, yet most of the blank-seal offenders ultimately could not escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 方徵，字可久，莆田人。

translations.literal: Fang Zheng, courtesy name Kejiu, was a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Zheng, styled Kejiu, was a native of Putian.

sentences.zh: 以鄉舉授給事中。

translations.literal: Recommended through the provincial examination, he was appointed Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended through the provincial examination, he was appointed Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍遊後苑，與聯詩句。

translations.literal: Once while attending the Emperor on an outing to the rear garden, they composed linked verses together.
translations.idiomatic: Once while attending the Emperor on an outing to the rear garden, they composed linked verses together.

sentences.zh: 太祖知其有母在，賜白金，馳驛歸省。

translations.literal: Taizu learned that he still had his mother living, granted him silver, and sent him by post-horses to visit her.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu learned that his mother was still living, granted him silver, and sent him by post-horses to visit her.

sentences.zh: 還改監察御史，出為懷慶知府。

translations.literal: On his return he was transferred to investigating censor and sent out as Prefect of Huaiqing.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was transferred to investigating censor and sent out as prefect of Huaiqing.

sentences.zh: 徵誌節甚偉，遇事敢直言。

translations.literal: Zheng's resolve and integrity were great; confronted with affairs he dared speak bluntly.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's resolve and integrity were formidable; when confronted with affairs he dared speak bluntly.

sentences.zh: 居郡時，因星變求言，疏言：「風憲官以激濁揚清為職。

translations.literal: When governing the prefecture, during a stellar anomaly that prompted calls for counsel, he submitted a memorial saying: "Censorial officials have as their duty to stir the turbid and elevate the clear.
translations.idiomatic: While governing the prefecture, during a stellar anomaly that prompted calls for counsel, he submitted a memorial saying: "Censorial officials have as their duty to stir the turbid and elevate the clear.

sentences.zh: 今不聞旌廉拔能，專務羅織人罪，多征贓罰，此大患也。

translations.literal: Now one hears nothing of honoring integrity and elevating talent; they devote themselves solely to fabricating charges against men and exacting much confiscation fines—this is a grave harm.
translations.idiomatic: Now one hears nothing of honoring integrity and elevating talent; they devote themselves solely to fabricating charges and exacting heavy confiscation fines—this is a grave evil.

sentences.zh: 朝廷賞罰明信，乃能勸懲。

translations.literal: When court rewards and punishments are clear and trusted, only then can encouragement and warning take effect.
translations.idiomatic: When court rewards and punishments are clear and trusted, only then can encouragement and warning take effect.

sentences.zh: 去年各行省官吏以用空印罹重罪，而河南參政安然、山東參政朱芾俱有空印，反遷布政使，何以示勸懲？

translations.literal: Last year officials of the various provinces suffered heavy punishment for using blank seals, yet Assistant Administers An Ran of Henan and Zhu Fei of Shandong both had blank seals and were instead transferred to become provincial administrators—how does this display encouragement and warning?
translations.idiomatic: Last year officials of the various provinces suffered heavy punishment for using blank seals, yet Assistant Administers An Ran of Henan and Zhu Fei of Shandong both had blank seals and were instead promoted to provincial administrators—how does this display encouragement and warning?

sentences.zh: 」帝問羅織及多征贓罰者為誰，徵指河南僉事彭京以對。

translations.literal: " The Emperor asked who fabricated charges and exacted excessive confiscation fines; Zheng pointed to Surveillance Vice Commissioner Peng Jing of Henan in reply.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor asked who fabricated charges and exacted excessive confiscation fines; Zheng pointed to Surveillance Vice Commissioner Peng Jing of Henan in reply.

sentences.zh: 貶沁陽驛丞。

translations.literal: He was demoted to post station chief of Qinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to post station chief of Qinyang.

sentences.zh: 十三年，以事逮至京，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was seized over some matter and brought to the capital, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was seized over some matter and brought to the capital, where he died.

sentences.zh: 周敬心，山東人，太學生也。

translations.literal: Zhou Jingxin, a native of Shandong, was a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jingxin, a native of Shandong, was a student of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十五年，詔求曉歷數者，敬心上疏極諫，且及時政數事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Hongwu an edict sought those versed in calendrical astronomy; Jingxin submitted a forthright memorial of extreme remonstrance, touching also on several current policies.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Hongwu an edict sought those versed in calendrical astronomy; Jingxin submitted a forthright memorial of extreme remonstrance, touching also on several matters of current policy.

sentences.zh: 略曰：

translations.literal: In summary it said:
translations.idiomatic: In summary, it read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞國祚長短，在德厚薄，不在歷數。

translations.literal: I have heard that whether a state's fortune is long or short depends on the thickness or thinness of virtue, not on calendrical fate.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the length of a dynasty's reign depends on the quality of its virtue, not on what the calendars foretell.

sentences.zh: 三代尚矣，三代而下，最久莫如漢、唐、宋，最短莫如秦、隋、五代。

translations.literal: The Three Dynasties are loftiest; below the Three Dynasties, none lasted so long as Han, Tang, and Song, and none so short as Qin, Sui, and the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dynasties stand at the summit of antiquity. Of all reigns since then, none endured so long as Han, Tang, and Song; none collapsed so quickly as Qin, Sui, and the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 其久也以有道，其短也以無道。

translations.literal: Their length came through having the Way; their shortness came through lacking the Way.
translations.idiomatic: They endured because they upheld the Way; they perished because they abandoned it.

sentences.zh: 陛下膺天眷命，救亂誅暴。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has received Heaven's favoring mandate, rescued disorder, and punished cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has received Heaven's mandate, quelled chaos, and punished the cruel.

sentences.zh: 然神武威斷則有余，寬大忠厚則不足。

translations.literal: Yet in divine martial awe and resolute judgment there is surplus; in magnanimity and loyal forbearance there is insufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you are more than sufficient in majesty and martial decisiveness, and not yet sufficient in magnanimity and loyal forbearance.

sentences.zh: 陛下若效兩漢之寬大，唐、宋之忠厚，講三代所以有道之長，則帝王之祚可傳萬世，何必問諸小道之人耶？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would emulate the magnanimity of the Two Han, the loyal forbearance of Tang and Song, and expound what made the Three Dynasties long in having the Way, then the emperor's fortune could be transmitted through ten thousand generations—why need one inquire of petty-path men?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would emulate the generosity of the Han dynasties and the steadfast loyalty of Tang and Song, and study what made the Three Dynasties endure, then the imperial throne could pass down through ten thousand generations. Why consult petty fortune-tellers?

sentences.zh: 臣又聞陛下連年遠征，北出沙漠，為恥不得傳國璽耳。

translations.literal: I have also heard that Your Majesty year after year campaigns far away, going north beyond the desert, solely from shame at not obtaining the Imperial Seal of succession.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that Your Majesty campaigns far afield year after year, marching north into the deserts—all for shame at not yet possessing the Imperial Seal.

sentences.zh: 昔楚平王時，琢卞和之玉，至秦始名為「璽」，歷代遞嬗，以訖後唐。

translations.literal: Formerly in the time of King Ping of Chu, Bian He's jade was carved; only from Qin was it named the 'Seal'; dynasty after dynasty it passed in succession, until Later Tang.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of King Ping of Chu, Bian He's jade was first carved into a seal; only under Qin did it receive the name 'Seal.' It passed from dynasty to dynasty down to Later Tang.

sentences.zh: 治亂興廢，皆不在此。

translations.literal: Order and disorder, rise and fall—none of it lay in this.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a state prospered or fell had nothing to do with it.

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭亂，潞王攜以自焚，則秦璽固已毀矣。

translations.literal: When Shi Jingtang brought disorder, the Prince of Lu carried it and burned himself with it—thus the Qin Seal was already destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Jingtang threw the realm into chaos, the Prince of Lu carried the seal with him into the fire and perished—and with him the Qin seal was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭入洛，更以玉制。

translations.literal: Jingtang entered Luoyang and had a new one made of jade.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingtang entered Luoyang, a new seal was fashioned from jade.

sentences.zh: 晉亡入遼，遼亡遺於桑乾河。

translations.literal: When Jin perished it entered Liao; when Liao perished it was left on the Sanggan River.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin fell, the seal passed to Liao; when Liao fell, it was lost in the Sanggan River.

sentences.zh: 元世祖時，劄剌爾者漁而得之。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Shizu of Yuan, one Zhalaer obtained it while fishing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizu of Yuan, a man named Zhalaer pulled it from the river while fishing.

sentences.zh: 今元人所挾，石氏璽耳。

translations.literal: What the Yuan men now carry is merely the Shi family's seal.
translations.idiomatic: The seal the Yuan now possess is nothing but the Shi family's replacement.

sentences.zh: 昔者三代不知有璽，仁為之璽，故曰「聖人大寶曰位，何以守位曰仁。

translations.literal: Formerly the Three Dynasties did not know there was a seal; benevolence served as the seal—thus it is said, 'The sage's great treasure is the throne; by what does one guard the throne? By benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Three Dynasties knew no seal; benevolence was their seal. Hence the maxim: 'The sage's greatest treasure is the throne; by what does one keep the throne? By benevolence.

sentences.zh: 」陛下奈何忽天下之大璽，而求漢、唐、宋之小璽也？

translations.literal: ' Why does Your Majesty neglect the great seal of all under Heaven and seek the petty seals of Han, Tang, and Song?
translations.idiomatic: ' Why, then, does Your Majesty overlook the great seal of all under Heaven and chase after the petty jade seals of Han, Tang, and Song?

sentences.zh: 方今力役過煩，賦斂過厚。

translations.literal: At present corvée labor is excessively burdensome; taxation and collection are excessively heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Today corvée labor is crushing, and taxes are oppressively heavy.

sentences.zh: 教化溥而民不悅；

translations.literal: Educative transformation is broad yet the people are not pleased;
translations.idiomatic: Though instruction reaches everywhere, the people are not content;

sentences.zh: 法度嚴而民不從。

translations.literal: laws and standards are strict yet the people do not follow.
translations.idiomatic: though the laws are stern, the people will not obey.

sentences.zh: 昔汲黯言於武帝曰：「陛下內多欲而外施仁義，奈何欲效唐、虞之治乎？

translations.literal: Formerly Ji An spoke to Emperor Wu, saying: 'Within, Your Majesty has many desires; outwardly you bestow benevolence and righteousness—how then can you wish to emulate the governance of Tang and Yu?
translations.idiomatic: Ji An once said to Emperor Wu, 'Your Majesty is full of desire within, yet displays benevolence and righteousness without—how can you hope to match the rule of Yao and Shun?

sentences.zh: 」方今國則願富，兵則願強，城池則願高深，宮室則願壯麗，土地則願廣，人民則願眾。

translations.literal: ' At present the state wishes to be rich, the army wishes to be strong, city walls wish to be high and deep, palaces wish to be grand and splendid, territory wishes to be broad, and the people wish to be numerous.
translations.idiomatic: ' Today you wish the treasury full and the army strong, the walls high and deep, the palaces grand, the territory vast, and the population numerous.

sentences.zh: 於是多取軍卒，廣籍資財，征伐不休，營造無極，如之何其可治也？

translations.literal: Accordingly one takes many soldiers and conscripts, widely registers wealth and goods, campaigns without cease, and constructs without limit—how then can it be governed?
translations.idiomatic: So you conscript ever more men, seize ever more wealth, campaign without rest, and build without end. How can such a state be governed?

sentences.zh: 臣又見洪武四年錄天下官吏，十三年連坐胡黨，十九年逮官吏積年為民害者，二十三年罪妄言者。

translations.literal: I also see that in the fourth year of Hongwu all officials under Heaven were recorded; in the thirteenth year punishment extended to Hu's faction by association; in the nineteenth year officials who for years had harmed the people were arrested; in the twenty-third year those who spoke rashly were punished.
translations.idiomatic: I also see that in the fourth year of Hongwu all officials in the realm were registered; in the thirteenth year mass punishment fell on Hu Weiyong's faction; in the nineteenth year officials who had long preyed on the people were seized; in the twenty-third year those who spoke unwisely were condemned.

sentences.zh: 大戮官民，不分臧否。

translations.literal: Great slaughter of officials and people, without distinction between good and bad.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike were slaughtered without distinction between the guilty and the innocent.

sentences.zh: 其中豈無忠臣、烈士、善人、君子？

translations.literal: Among them, could there have been no loyal ministers, martyrs, good men, or gentlemen?
translations.idiomatic: Surely among them were loyal ministers, martyrs, good men, and upright gentlemen?

sentences.zh: 於茲見陛下之薄德而任刑矣。

translations.literal: From this one sees Your Majesty's thin virtue and reliance on punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In this one sees Your Majesty's meager virtue and your reliance on harsh punishment.

sentences.zh: 水旱連年，夫豈無故哉！

translations.literal: Floods and droughts year after year—how could this be without cause!
translations.idiomatic: Floods and droughts strike year after year—is there no reason for this?

sentences.zh: 言皆激切。

translations.literal: His words were all sharp and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Every line was sharp and impassioned.

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: A report was received.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received.

sentences.zh: 王樸，同州人。

translations.literal: Wang Pu was a native of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu was a native of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武十八年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the eighteenth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the eighteenth year of Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 本名權，帝為改焉。

translations.literal: His original name was Quan; the Emperor changed it for him.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Quan; the Emperor gave him a new name.

sentences.zh: 除吏科給事中，以直諫忤旨罷。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supervising Secretary in the Personnel Section, but was dismissed for forthright remonstrance that offended the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Supervising Secretary in the Personnel Section, but was dismissed after forthright remonstrance offended the throne.

sentences.zh: 旋起御史。

translations.literal: Shortly he was reappointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 陳時事千余言。

translations.literal: He presented current affairs in more than a thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial of more than a thousand words on affairs of the day.

sentences.zh: 性鯁直，數與帝辨是非，不肯屈。

translations.literal: By nature upright and blunt, he often debated right and wrong with the Emperor and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt and unyielding by nature, he often argued with the Emperor over right and wrong and refused to back down.

sentences.zh: 一日，遇事爭之強。

translations.literal: One day, encountering some matter, he disputed it fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: One day he argued his point with unusual force on some matter.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命戮之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angered and ordered him executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage and ordered him executed.

sentences.zh: 及市，召還，諭之曰：「汝其改乎？

translations.literal: At the execution ground, he was summoned back and instructed, saying: 'Will you change?
translations.idiomatic: At the execution ground he was called back and asked, 'Will you change your ways?

sentences.zh: 」樸對曰：「陛下不以臣為不肖，擢官御史，奈何摧辱至此！

translations.literal: ' Pu replied: 'Your Majesty did not regard me as unworthy and promoted me to investigating censor—why humiliate and insult me to this point!
translations.idiomatic: ' Pu answered, 'Your Majesty did not deem me unworthy when you made me investigating censor—why degrade me like this!

sentences.zh: 使臣無罪，安得戮之？

translations.literal: If your subject is without crime, how can you execute him?
translations.idiomatic: If I am guiltless, how can Your Majesty put me to death?

sentences.zh: 有罪，又安用生之？

translations.literal: If guilty, what use is there in keeping me alive?
translations.idiomatic: If I am guilty, why recall me only to let me live?

sentences.zh: 臣今日願速死耳。

translations.literal: Your subject today only wishes to die quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Today I ask only to die quickly.

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，趣命行刑。

translations.literal: ' The Emperor was greatly angered and urgently ordered the execution carried out.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Emperor's fury boiled over, and he commanded that the sentence be carried out at once.

sentences.zh: 過史館，大呼曰：「學士劉三吾誌之：某年月日，皇帝殺無罪御史樸也！

translations.literal: Passing the Historiography Institute, he shouted loudly: 'Academician Liu Sanwu, record this: on such-and-such year, month, and day, the Emperor killed the guiltless investigating censor Pu!
translations.idiomatic: Passing the Historiography Institute, he cried out, 'Academician Liu Sanwu, take this down: on such-and-such day the Emperor executed the guiltless censor Pu!

sentences.zh: 」竟戮死。

translations.literal: ' In the end he was executed to death.
translations.idiomatic: ' And so he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 帝撰《大誥》，謂樸誹謗，猶列其名。

translations.literal: The Emperor compiled the Grand Pronouncements, saying Pu had slandered, yet still listed his name.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor compiled the Grand Pronouncements, charging Pu with slander, he still listed his name.

sentences.zh: 有張衡者，萬安人，樸同年進士。

translations.literal: There was one Zhang Heng, a native of Wan'an, a metropolitan graduate in the same year as Pu.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Zhang Heng, a native of Wan'an and a fellow metropolitan graduate of Pu's year.

sentences.zh: 授禮科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supervising Secretary in the Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Supervising Secretary in the Rites Section.

sentences.zh: 奏疏剴切。

translations.literal: His memorials were earnest and sharp.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials were earnest and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 擢禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 以清慎見褒，載於《大誥》。

translations.literal: For purity and caution he was praised, and this was recorded in the Grand Pronouncements.
translations.idiomatic: He was commended for integrity and prudence, and his example was recorded in the Grand Pronouncements.

sentences.zh: 後亦以言事坐死。

translations.literal: Later he also was put to death on account of speaking on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He too was later executed for speaking out on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：太祖英武威斷，廷臣奏對，往往失辭。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Taizu was heroic and martial with decisive awe; when court ministers submitted responses in memorials, they often lost proper words.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Taizu was formidable and decisive; court ministers often lost their footing when answering his questions.

sentences.zh: 而錢唐、韓宜可、李仕魯輩，抱其樸誠，力諍於堂陛間，可謂古之遺直矣。

translations.literal: Yet Qian Tang, Han Yike, Li Shilu, and their kind, holding to their plain sincerity, strove to remonstrate between hall and steps, and may be called the remnant upright men of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qian Tang, Han Yike, Li Shilu, and men like them held fast to plain sincerity and remonstrated boldly before the throne—they may be called the last heirs of the upright ministers of old.

sentences.zh: 伯巨、敬心以縫掖諸生，言天下至計，雖違於信而後諫之義，然原厥本心，由於忠愛。

translations.literal: Boju and Jingxin, as girdled-sleeve academy students, spoke the utmost plans for all under Heaven; though this violated the principle of remonstrating only after trust is established, yet tracing their original heart, it arose from loyal love.
translations.idiomatic: Boju and Jingxin were mere academy students in scholar's robes who spoke on the weightiest matters of state. Though this violated the principle of remonstrating only once trust is established, their motives sprang from loyal devotion.

sentences.zh: 以視末季沽名賣直之流，有不可同日而語者也。

translations.literal: Compared with the stream of late-age men who trade on fame and sell uprightness, there is no speaking of them on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with the late-dynasty type who grandstand for reputation and perform integrity for profit, they belong to a different order altogether.
